$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and put for two homologues $a,b$

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad 0\le k\le5 , $$

the obligatory one–break, strand–asymmetric gamete.  On the $F_{1}$ 
$P_{0}/P_{1}$

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;,\;0\le k\le5\},
\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1 $$

is the $6$ monotone $0\to1$ $5$–mers

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111 $ .

An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and an $F_{3}$
gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$.  $a$ and $b$ are monotone non-decreasing, so
$R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and on $k+1\ldots5$.  Hence a
$+$–strand $F_{3}$ haplotype can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the
junction $k|k+1$.  Conversely every binary word of length $n$ which can
be written as a monotone prefix followed by a monotone suffix, i.e.
every word with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent, is of the form $R_{k}(a,b)$ with
$a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$.

Writing a word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent as

$$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=n,\;b>0,\;c>0 ,$$

put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0\}= \binom{n-2+4-1}{3}=\binom{n+1}{3}
$$

words have exactly one descent.  The $n+1$ monotone words $0^{k}1^{\,n-k}$
have zero descents.  Hence on the chosen orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

distinct $+$–strand haplotypes can be made after the two obligatory
single cross-overs $P\to F_{1}\to F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20, $$

i.e. the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the $20$ valley haplotypes

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0,
$$

e.g. $00101,01011,01101,\dots$  This is $6+20=26$ different
$+$–strand chromosomes in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.  The six $5$-mers
which need $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ and its complements, are
first reached in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and
$325$ heterozygous, the $6$ monotone haplotypes being the $F_{2}$ set.
Up to phase this is the usual $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one–descent
haplotype count, $6+20=26$ on the fixed $+$ strand, which is often
quoted as $22$ $s\le2$ words, $30=2^{5}-2$ words and $2^{5}=32$ words
when the two reciprocal orientations are allowed to be distinguished.

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and
write a directed meiosis as

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad 0\le k\le 5, $$

on the + strand.  With the fixed orientation the $F_{1}$ gametes are

$$S_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k}\equiv s_{k},\qquad 0\le k\le5, $$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ words

$$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,
$$

the $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with
$a,b\in S_{1}$ and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is again $R_{k}(a,b)$.
Writing $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$ and  $b=s_{t_{2}}=
0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$

$$r=R_{k}(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}\qquad 
t_{1}<k<t_{2} ,$$

i.e. up to the trivial monotone limits $k\le t_{1}$ and $k\ge t_{2}$ an
$F_{3}$ + strand word is a monotone prefix followed by a monotone
suffix.  Hence an $F_{3}$ + strand word can contain at most one
$1\to0$ descent and, if it does, the descent can be taken to be the
junction $k$.  In binary notation

$$r=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,c>0, $$

i.e. the words of length $5$ with $\le 1$ $1\to0$ descent.  With
$b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1$ the number of one-descent words is the number of
solutions of $a+b'+c'+d=3$,

$$N_{1}(n)=\binom{n+1}{3}, $$

and together with the $N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words

$$|S_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}
       =(n+1)\frac{n^{2}-n+6}{6} $$

distinct + strand haplotypes are attainable after the two directed
meioses $P\to F_{1}\to F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20, $$

so that

$$|S_{2}|=6+20=26$$

different + strand haplotypes can be seen in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.
They are the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes

$$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$$

and the 20 valley haplotypes $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with exactly one
$1\to0$ descent, e.g. $01011,00101,01101$, etc.  The two parental
haplotypes $00000$ and $11111$ are included.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\,26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes.  The six
monotone words are already present in $F_{2}$; the $20$ one-descent
words are new in $F_{3}$.  This is the usual $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$
one-descent count.  Up to phase the $2^{5}-2=30$ words with $\le3$
switches are obtained if the two reciprocal products of a crossover are
counted as distinct, the two alternating words $01010$ and $10101$ being
the only $5$-bit words which need two $1\to0$ descents and are first
reached in $F_{4}$.

Remark.  With the strictly interior obligatory crossover
$1\le k\le4$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the four interior monotone mosaics
$01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the $F_{3}$ + strand pool is the
$0\!-\!1$–fixed set

$$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,
$$

$2^{\,n-2}=8$ distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. $8\cdot9/2=36$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the $2^{m-2}$ textbook limit.
∎

17.text:
On the + strand put $P_{0}=00000$, $P_{1}=11111$ and write the directed
one–break

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5}\qquad 0\le k\le 5 ,
$$

for a gamete made from the homologues $a,b$.  Up to the sign of the
strand the $F_{1}$ heterozygote is $P_{0}/P_{1}$ and

$$
{\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}
$$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\!\to\!1$ words

$$
11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000 .
$$

Every $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$ with $a=s_{t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}$, $s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  After relabelling $t_{1}\le t_{2}$

* $k\le t_{1}$ gives $R_{k}=s_{t_{2}}$,
* $k\ge t_{2}$ gives $R_{k}=s_{t_{1}}$,
* $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$ gives

$$
R_{k}(s_{t_{1}},s_{t_{2}})=0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},
$$

so that $R_{k}$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on $k+1\ldots5$.
Hence an $F_{3}$ +–strand haplotype can contain at most one $1\to0$
descent and, if it does, the descent can be taken at the cut $k$.
Up to relabelling

$$
w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0,
$$

i.e. $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with the conventional $a+b'+c'+d=5-2$.
Put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$.  The number of essentially distinct
one–descent words is

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

and

$$
N_{0}(n)=n+1
$$

is the monotone set.  Hence on the chosen orientation

$$
|{\cal H}_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

is the set of +–strand haplotypes that can be present as an $F_{3}$
chromosome, i.e. as the gametes formed in the $F_{2}$ meiosis.
For $n=5$

$$
N_{0}=6\;:\;00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111,
$$

$$
N_{1}= \binom{6}{3}=20
$$

one–descent words $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$t_{1}<k<t_{2}$, e.g. $00101,01011,11000$, etc.  Altogether

$$
|{\cal H}_{2}|=6+20=26
$$

different $5$-bit +–strand haplotypes can be segregating in the $F_{3}$
generation, the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes and twenty new
valley haplotypes.  The six words that need $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $10101$, are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes.  This is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ directed one–break closure.  If the two
reciprocal phases of the $F_{1}$ heterozygote are counted as distinct
the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ +–strand haplotypes,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes, are obtained. ∎

11.text:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\equiv00000$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}\equiv11111$

and put for a pair $a,b$

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\dots k}b_{k+1\dots5}\qquad0\le k\le5$

for the oriented one break product which is seen on the $+$ strand.
Modulo the $0\leftrightarrow1$ phase the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}
      =\{11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000\}, $$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ haplotypes.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is a
member of ${\cal H}_{1}$ and in particular contains no $1\to0$ descent.

Let $a=0^{p}1^{5-p}$, $b=0^{q}1^{5-q}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)_{i}=a_{i}\;(i\le k),\;R_{k}(a,b)_{i}=b_{i}\;(i>k)$,

so that the left block $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and the right block
$R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both monotone.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand
haplotype can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$.
Conversely every binary word of length $n$ with at most one $1\to0$
descent can be written in the form

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=n,\;b>0\lor c=0 $

with $b>0$, $c>0$ for the non-monotone case.  With $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  The $N_{0}(n)=n+1$ monotone
words are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Hence, up to the fixed $0\to1$ orientation,

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}(n)+N_{1}(n)=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct $+$ strand haploid sequences can be made by two successive
oriented one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,\qquad |{\cal H}_{3}|=6+20=26,$

the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the $20$ valley haplotypes
$0^{p}1^{k-p}0^{\,q-k}1^{\,5-q}$, $p<k<q$, e.g. $00101,01011,01101$, etc.,
which are the $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gametes.  In particular the $32$ binary
words are one descent short of saturation; the six words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ different haploid
sequences on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand.  This is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent limit.  With the strictly interior
obligate break $1\le k\le4$ the parental $k=0,5$ classes are removed and
the attainable $+$ strand set is $0\ldots01$, $|{\cal H}_{3}^{{\rm int}}|
=2^{\,n-2}=8$, viz. $00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, the
usual $2^{n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit. ∎

18.text:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}$, $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and for a directed single break put

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad 0\le k\le5$ ,
the left block being taken from the first homologue and the right block
from the second homologue.  Up to the arbitrary choice of the $+$
strand the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is the monotone $0\to1$
pool

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{\,5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone chromosomes
$a_{k}=00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is an element of ${\cal H}_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$h=R_{k}(a,b)$, $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ .

Writing $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ and
$t_{1}\le t_{2}$,

$R_{k}(a,b)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
a ,&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
b ,&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},\;&t_{1}<k<t_{2},
\end{array}\right.$

so that on the $+$ strand a $F_{3}$ gamete is a monotone word on the
left of the cut and a monotone word on the right of the cut.  Hence a
$F_{3}$ $+$ strand word can contain at most one $1\to0$ descent and it
can be written uniquely as

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,$

with the monotone case $c=0$.  Putting $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$ the number
of one-descent words is the number of solutions of
$a+b'+c'+d=5-2$ in four non–negative variables,

$N_{1}(5)=\binom{5-2+4-1}{3}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

and the $N_{0}=5+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Hence with the formal terminal
cuts $k=0,5$ allowed

$\bigl|{\cal H}_{2}\bigr|=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be present as a chromosome in the
$F_{3}$ population, the six monotone
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$ and the twenty valley
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  In diploid terms this is
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes.  The $20$ valley haplotypes are the $F_{3}$-specific
$0\to1\to0\to1$ mosaics, e.g. $00101=001|01$,
$01011=01|011$, etc.; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$01010,10101,\dots$, are first reached in $F_{4}$.

In particular with a strictly obligate internal break
$1\le k\le4$ the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four interior monotone
haplotypes $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the directed $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
pool is the eight start-$0$ end-$1$ $+$ strand haplotypes

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101,$

i.e. the $2^{3}=8$ strings $0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1$ with at most one
$1\to0$ descent, the usual $8$–haplotype, $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered
diploid genotype, limit of a strictly obligate single oriented
crossover.  Adding back the formal terminal products $k=0,5$ this is
the $6+20=26$ haplotype $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count quoted above.

16.text:
On the + strand the two founders can be written as

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$
and with a single, orientation fixed crossover a gamete which is made
from a pair $a,b$ is

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}\,,\qquad 0\le k\le 5 .$$

On the $F_{1}$ the two homologues are $A/B$ and, with the orientation
fixed on the $+$ strand,

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ haplotypes

$$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000  .$$

In particular every $F_{1}$ gamete and therefore every $F_{2}$
chromosome is monotone non-decreasing and contains no $1\to0$ descent.
Put $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.
Then

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}
$$

so that an $F_{3}$ gamete is the juxtaposition of a monotone left block
and a monotone right block.  Hence an $F_{3}$ gamete can contain at
most one $1\to0$ descent and the descent, if it is present, is forced
to be the junction $k\mid k+1$ of the crossover.  Up to the fixed
orientation a word with one descent is

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0 ,$$

and with $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}= \binom{n+1}{3}.$$

For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=n+1=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20 $$

so that on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

different haploid sequences can be made in the gametes that form the
$F_{3}$.  For $n=5$

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=6+20=26$$

distinct positive-strand haplotypes, the six monotone
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the $20$ one-descent
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes, e.g. $00101=001\;|\;01$, can be
present in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.  The six $5$-bit words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., are first reached in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, attainable on the $+$ strand.  This is the usual
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count; with the two phases identified
it is the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ positive-strand words with $\le3$ runs,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes, quoted in the
phase-unrestricted literature. ∎

public_text.8:
The asymmetry is the key. The problem explicitly says we are considering only the arbitrarily positive strand and that recombination is allowed in only one orientation. On that strand a meiosis is

R_k(a,b)= a_{1..k} b_{k+1..5}

with the left block always coming from the same homologue in the ordered pair.  Hence phase matters.

In P the two homologues are 00000 and 11111.  The F1 heterozygote is therefore 00000 / 11111 and its gametes on the + strand are

R_k(00000,11111)=0^{k}1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5,

i.e. the six monotone non-decreasing words

11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000.

The reciprocal 1^{k}0^{5-k} products are the same physical event read on the opposite strand and are not counted separately once the strand is fixed.  That is the F1/F2 haplotype pool.

An F2 individual is a pair a=s_{t1}, b=s_{t2} with s_t=0^{t}1^{5-t}.  An F3 gamete is again R_k(a,b).  With t1≤t2

* k≤t1 → R_k(a,b)=s_{t2}
* k≥t2 → R_k(a,b)=s_{t1}
* t1<k<t2 → R_k(a,b)=0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2}.

So the only non-monotone words that can appear are of the form

0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5, b>0,c>0,

i.e. binary words of length 5 with exactly one 1→0 descent.  The monotone words are the zero-descent case.

Put b'=b-1, c'=c-1. Then a+b'+c'+d=3 with a,b',c',d≥0.  The number of solutions is C(3+4-1,3)=C(6,3)=20.  Adding the n+1=6 monotone words gives

6+20=26

distinct + strand haplotypes in the F3 gamete pool.  Up to ordering the diploid count is 26·27/2=351.

The 30 count is obtained by letting the F1 also generate the 1^{k}0^{5-k} products as distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. by allowing both phases of the F1 heterozygote on the same arbitrarily chosen strand.  With the stated strand asymmetry those reciprocal products are the same sequence on the opposite strand and must not be double counted.  Once the orientation is fixed the six words that need ≥2 1→0 descents, e.g. 10101, 01010, etc., are unreachable in F3 and the attainable set is the 26 one-descent words above. ∎
public_text.2:
The asymmetry is the key.  On the arbitrarily chosen positive strand the
recombinant that is transmitted from a heterozygote a/b is the ordered
mosaic

R_k(a,b)= a_{1..k} b_{k+1..5},  0 ≤ k ≤5 ,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The first meiosis is 00000/11111.  With the orientation fixed the only
gametes that are seen on the positive strand are

R_k(00000,11111)=0^{k}1^{5-k},    k=0…5,

the six monotone 0…01…1 strings

11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000.

The reciprocal products 1^{k}0^{5-k} are the same physical recombinants
seen on the complementary strand.  Counting them on the positive strand
is double counting the reciprocal products that the stated asymmetry
forbids.  Hence |S1|=6 on the chosen strand, not 10, and every F2
haplotype is monotone non-decreasing.

An F2 individual is therefore a pair s_t , s_u with s_t=0^{t}1^{5-t}.
A gamete made in the F2→F3 meiosis is R_k(s_t,s_u).  Write t ≤ u.
* k ≤ t gives R_k=s_u,
* k ≥ u gives R_k=s_t,
* t<k<u gives

r=0^{t}1^{k-t}0^{u-k}1^{5-u}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},

a+b+c+d=5, b>0,c>0.

Thus on the positive strand an F3 haplotype is the concatenation of a
monotone left part and a monotone right part.  The only 1→0 descent
that can appear is the one that may sit at the junction k|k+1.  In
particular an F3 haplotype has ≤1 1→0 descent.

The monotone words are n+1=6.  A word with exactly one 1→0 descent at
position p is monotone on the left and monotone on the right, i.e.
0^{a}1^{p-a}0^{c}1^{d} with a<p, c>0.  Up to the choice of the two
parents this is p(5-p) words for fixed p.  Summing

∑_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=1·4+2·3+3·2+4·1=20

one-descent words, e.g. 00101=001|01= pref3(00111)+suff2(00001).
Hence

|H3|=N0+N1=(n+1)+∑p p(n-p)=6+20=26

distinct positive-strand haplotypes, the six F2 monotone haplotypes

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}

descents, e.g. $10101$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal
$F_{3}$ chromosomes and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$ heterozygous.  This is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation fixed, count, $6+20=26$
haploid +–strand sequences.  Allowing the two reciprocal $F_{1}$
orientations the usual $2^{5}-2=30$ $+$–strand words with $\le3$
switches are obtained. ∎
public_text.1:
On the + strand write the two founders

* $A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$  .

With the orientation fixed a gamete which is made from a pair $x,y$
is

\begin{equation*}
R_{k}(x,y)=x_{1..k}y_{k+1..5},\qquad0\le k\le 5 ,
\end{equation*}
the left block being taken from the first homologue and the right block
from the second.

$F_{1}$ .  $A/B$ gives on the + strand

\begin{equation*}
{\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\},
\qquad|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6,
\end{equation*}
the six monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone and contains no
$1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ .  Let $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$ and
$c=R_{k}(a,b)$.  Then $c_{1..k}$ and $c_{k+1..5}$ are monotone.  Hence
$c$ can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k$ and

\begin{equation*}
c=
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},\qquad
t_{1}\le k\le t_{2},
\end{equation*}
i.e. up to the trivial $t_{1}\ge k$ or $t_{2}\le k$ cases
$c=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0$.
Putting $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$,

$a+b'+c'+d=5-2$

so that the number of one–descent words is

\begin{equation*}
N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3},
\end{equation*}
the $n+1$ monotone words being $N_{0}(n)=n+1$.  Hence on the chosen
+ strand the gametic pool which forms the $F_{3}$ is

\begin{equation*}
|{\cal H}_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3},\qquad
n=5,
\end{equation*}
i.e.

$N_{0}=6$ monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ haplotypes

$N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$ one–descent words
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\;b>0,c>0$, e.g. $00101=001\,|\,01$,

in all

$|{\cal H}_{2}|=6+20=26$

different +–strand haplotypes that can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome.  The six monotone words are already present in $F_{2}$,
the 20 valley words, $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, are new in $F_{3}$.  The $2^{5}=32$ binary
words are one descent short of saturation; the six words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal and
$\,26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, 26
homozygous and $325$ heterozygous, the $26$ haplotypes being the
conventional $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count.  Up to the
conventional reciprocal phase this is the $30=2^{5}-2$ +/– strand
count $2\sum_{s=0}^{3}\binom{4}{s}$ and the $465$ unordered diploid
genotypes usually quoted. ∎
public_text.12:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5} , $$

and write a directed single–crossover gamete produced from a pair
$a,b$ as

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5}\qquad 0\le k\le5 .$$

In particular

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}\;:\;0\le t\le5\}$
is the F$_{1}$ gametic pool.  Up to the chosen $+$ orientation every
F$_{2}$ chromosome is monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  Hence an F$_{2}$ individual
is $s_{t_{a}}/s_{t_{b}}$ and an F$_{2}\to$F$_{3}$ gamete is
$R_{k}(s_{t_{a}},s_{t_{b}})$.  For $t_{a}\le t_{b}$

* $k\le t_{a}$ : $R_{k}=s_{t_{b}}$,
* $k\ge t_{b}$ : $R_{k}=s_{t_{a}}$,
* $t_{a}<k<t_{b}$ :

$$
R_{k}(s_{t_{a}},s_{t_{b}})=0^{t_{a}}1^{\,k-t_{a}}0^{\,t_{b}-k}1^{\,5-t_{b}}
     =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0 ,
$$

i.e. a word whose left $k$–block and right $5-k$–block are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  The only $1\to0$ descent that can be created in
the F$_{2}\to$F$_{3}$ meiosis is the descent at the junction $k|k+1$.

The monotone, zero-descent words are

$$N_{0}=n+1=6,\qquad s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t},\qquad 0\le t\le5,
$$

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
A word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent is $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with
$b\ge1,c\ge1$.  Put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1$.  Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}.$$

For $n=5$

$$N_{1}(5)=\binom{6}{3}=20$$

one-descent words, e.g. $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$.  Hence the set of $+$–strand haplotypes that
can be made by two successive directed obligatory cross-overs, i.e. the
haploid material that can be present in the F$_{3}$ chromosomes, is

$$
|S_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

and for $n=5$

$$|S_{2}|=6+20=26$$

different $+$ strand haploid sequences.  Six of them are the F$_{2}$
monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes and $20$ are the new one-descent
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The six $2^{5}$ words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$, are first reachable in F$_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  Up to order there
are $26\cdot27/2=351$ distinct unordered F$_{3}$ autosomal genotypes,
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\,\times\,$ paternal genotypes.  The
$6$ monotone haplotypes are the F$_{2}$ pool; the $20$ one-descent
haplotypes are the new F$_{3}$ haplotypes.  This is the usual
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count, $6+20=26$ on the strictly
orientation-fixed $+$ strand, $30=2^{5}-2$ and $22=2\sum_{s=0}^{2}
\binom{4}{s}$ when the two reciprocal F$_{1}$ phases are kept distinct.
public_text.15:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the two founders as
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and put for two homologues $a,b$

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad 0\le k\le5 , $$

the obligatory one–break, strand–asymmetric gamete.  On the $F_{1}$ 
$P_{0}/P_{1}$

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;,\;0\le k\le5\},
\qquad |{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1 $$

is the $6$ monotone $0\to1$ $5$–mers

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111 $ .

An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and an $F_{3}$
gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$.  $a$ and $b$ are monotone non-decreasing, so
$R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and on $k+1\ldots5$.  Hence a
$+$–strand $F_{3}$ haplotype can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the
junction $k|k+1$.  Conversely every binary word of length $n$ which can
be written as a monotone prefix followed by a monotone suffix, i.e.
every word with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent, is of the form $R_{k}(a,b)$ with
$a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$.

Writing a word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent as

$$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=n,\;b>0,\;c>0 ,$$

put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0\}= \binom{n-2+4-1}{3}=\binom{n+1}{3}
$$

words have exactly one descent.  The $n+1$ monotone words $0^{k}1^{\,n-k}$
have zero descents.  Hence on the chosen orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

distinct $+$–strand haplotypes can be made after the two obligatory
single cross-overs $P\to F_{1}\to F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20, $$

i.e. the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the $20$ valley haplotypes

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0,
$$

e.g. $00101,01011,01101,\dots$  This is $6+20=26$ different
$+$–strand chromosomes in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.  The six $5$-mers
which need $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $01010$ and its complements, are
first reached in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and
$325$ heterozygous, the $6$ monotone haplotypes being the $F_{2}$ set.
Up to phase this is the usual $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one–descent
haplotype count, $6+20=26$ on the fixed $+$ strand, which is often
quoted as $22$ $s\le2$ words, $30=2^{5}-2$ words and $2^{5}=32$ words
when the two reciprocal orientations are allowed to be distinguished.
public_text.4:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and
write a directed meiosis as

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad 0\le k\le 5, $$

on the + strand.  With the fixed orientation the $F_{1}$ gametes are

$$S_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k}\equiv s_{k},\qquad 0\le k\le5, $$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ words

$$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,
$$

the $F_{2}$ haplotype pool.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with
$a,b\in S_{1}$ and an $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is again $R_{k}(a,b)$.
Writing $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$ and  $b=s_{t_{2}}=
0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$

$$r=R_{k}(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}\qquad 
t_{1}<k<t_{2} ,$$

i.e. up to the trivial monotone limits $k\le t_{1}$ and $k\ge t_{2}$ an
$F_{3}$ + strand word is a monotone prefix followed by a monotone
suffix.  Hence an $F_{3}$ + strand word can contain at most one
$1\to0$ descent and, if it does, the descent can be taken to be the
junction $k$.  In binary notation

$$r=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,c>0, $$

i.e. the words of length $5$ with $\le 1$ $1\to0$ descent.  With
$b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1$ the number of one-descent words is the number of
solutions of $a+b'+c'+d=3$,

$$N_{1}(n)=\binom{n+1}{3}, $$

and together with the $N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words

$$|S_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}
       =(n+1)\frac{n^{2}-n+6}{6} $$

distinct + strand haplotypes are attainable after the two directed
meioses $P\to F_{1}\to F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20, $$

so that

$$|S_{2}|=6+20=26$$

different + strand haplotypes can be seen in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.
They are the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes

$$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$$

and the 20 valley haplotypes $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with exactly one
$1\to0$ descent, e.g. $01011,00101,01101$, etc.  The two parental
haplotypes $00000$ and $11111$ are included.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$\,26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes.  The six
monotone words are already present in $F_{2}$; the $20$ one-descent
words are new in $F_{3}$.  This is the usual $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$
one-descent count.  Up to phase the $2^{5}-2=30$ words with $\le3$
switches are obtained if the two reciprocal products of a crossover are
counted as distinct, the two alternating words $01010$ and $10101$ being
the only $5$-bit words which need two $1\to0$ descents and are first
reached in $F_{4}$.

Remark.  With the strictly interior obligatory crossover
$1\le k\le4$ the $F_{1}$ pool is the four interior monotone mosaics
$01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the $F_{3}$ + strand pool is the
$0\!-\!1$–fixed set

$$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111,
$$

$2^{\,n-2}=8$ distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. $8\cdot9/2=36$
unordered diploid $F_{3}$ autosomes, the $2^{m-2}$ textbook limit.
∎
public_text.17:
On the + strand put $P_{0}=00000$, $P_{1}=11111$ and write the directed
one–break

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5}\qquad 0\le k\le 5 ,
$$

for a gamete made from the homologues $a,b$.  Up to the sign of the
strand the $F_{1}$ heterozygote is $P_{0}/P_{1}$ and

$$
{\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{t}1^{5-t}:0\le t\le5\}
$$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\!\to\!1$ words

$$
11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000 .
$$

Every $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$ with $a=s_{t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}$, $s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  After relabelling $t_{1}\le t_{2}$

* $k\le t_{1}$ gives $R_{k}=s_{t_{2}}$,
* $k\ge t_{2}$ gives $R_{k}=s_{t_{1}}$,
* $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$ gives

$$
R_{k}(s_{t_{1}},s_{t_{2}})=0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},
$$

so that $R_{k}$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on $k+1\ldots5$.
Hence an $F_{3}$ +–strand haplotype can contain at most one $1\to0$
descent and, if it does, the descent can be taken at the cut $k$.
Up to relabelling

$$
w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0,
$$

i.e. $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with the conventional $a+b'+c'+d=5-2$.
Put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$.  The number of essentially distinct
one–descent words is

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

and

$$
N_{0}(n)=n+1
$$

is the monotone set.  Hence on the chosen orientation

$$
|{\cal H}_{2}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3},
$$

is the set of +–strand haplotypes that can be present as an $F_{3}$
chromosome, i.e. as the gametes formed in the $F_{2}$ meiosis.
For $n=5$

$$
N_{0}=6\;:\;00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111,
$$

$$
N_{1}= \binom{6}{3}=20
$$

one–descent words $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$t_{1}<k<t_{2}$, e.g. $00101,01011,11000$, etc.  Altogether

$$
|{\cal H}_{2}|=6+20=26
$$

different $5$-bit +–strand haplotypes can be segregating in the $F_{3}$
generation, the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes and twenty new
valley haplotypes.  The six words that need $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $10101$, are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes give $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes.  This is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ directed one–break closure.  If the two
reciprocal phases of the $F_{1}$ heterozygote are counted as distinct
the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ +–strand haplotypes,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes, are obtained. ∎
public_text.11:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}\equiv00000$ , $P_{1}=1^{5}\equiv11111$

and put for a pair $a,b$

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\dots k}b_{k+1\dots5}\qquad0\le k\le5$

for the oriented one break product which is seen on the $+$ strand.
Modulo the $0\leftrightarrow1$ phase the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}
      =\{11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000\}, $$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ haplotypes.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is a
member of ${\cal H}_{1}$ and in particular contains no $1\to0$ descent.

Let $a=0^{p}1^{5-p}$, $b=0^{q}1^{5-q}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)_{i}=a_{i}\;(i\le k),\;R_{k}(a,b)_{i}=b_{i}\;(i>k)$,

so that the left block $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and the right block
$R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both monotone.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand
haplotype can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$.
Conversely every binary word of length $n$ with at most one $1\to0$
descent can be written in the form

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=n,\;b>0\lor c=0 $

with $b>0$, $c>0$ for the non-monotone case.  With $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  The $N_{0}(n)=n+1$ monotone
words are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Hence, up to the fixed $0\to1$ orientation,

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}(n)+N_{1}(n)=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct $+$ strand haploid sequences can be made by two successive
oriented one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,\qquad |{\cal H}_{3}|=6+20=26,$

the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the $20$ valley haplotypes
$0^{p}1^{k-p}0^{\,q-k}1^{\,5-q}$, $p<k<q$, e.g. $00101,01011,01101$, etc.,
which are the $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gametes.  In particular the $32$ binary
words are one descent short of saturation; the six words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$
unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ different haploid
sequences on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand.  This is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent limit.  With the strictly interior
obligate break $1\le k\le4$ the parental $k=0,5$ classes are removed and
the attainable $+$ strand set is $0\ldots01$, $|{\cal H}_{3}^{{\rm int}}|
=2^{\,n-2}=8$, viz. $00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, the
usual $2^{n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit. ∎
public_text.18:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5}$, $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and for a directed single break put

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad 0\le k\le5$ ,
the left block being taken from the first homologue and the right block
from the second homologue.  Up to the arbitrary choice of the $+$
strand the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool is the monotone $0\to1$
pool

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{\,5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone chromosomes
$a_{k}=00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is an element of ${\cal H}_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is

$h=R_{k}(a,b)$, $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ .

Writing $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ and
$t_{1}\le t_{2}$,

$R_{k}(a,b)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
a ,&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
b ,&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},\;&t_{1}<k<t_{2},
\end{array}\right.$

so that on the $+$ strand a $F_{3}$ gamete is a monotone word on the
left of the cut and a monotone word on the right of the cut.  Hence a
$F_{3}$ $+$ strand word can contain at most one $1\to0$ descent and it
can be written uniquely as

$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,$

with the monotone case $c=0$.  Putting $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$ the number
of one-descent words is the number of solutions of
$a+b'+c'+d=5-2$ in four non–negative variables,

$N_{1}(5)=\binom{5-2+4-1}{3}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

and the $N_{0}=5+1=6$ monotone words
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.  Hence with the formal terminal
cuts $k=0,5$ allowed

$\bigl|{\cal H}_{2}\bigr|=N_{0}+N_{1}=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be present as a chromosome in the
$F_{3}$ population, the six monotone
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$ and the twenty valley
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  In diploid terms this is
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes.  The $20$ valley haplotypes are the $F_{3}$-specific
$0\to1\to0\to1$ mosaics, e.g. $00101=001|01$,
$01011=01|011$, etc.; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$01010,10101,\dots$, are first reached in $F_{4}$.

In particular with a strictly obligate internal break
$1\le k\le4$ the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ pool is the four interior monotone
haplotypes $01111,00111,00011,00001$ and the directed $F_{2}\to F_{3}$
pool is the eight start-$0$ end-$1$ $+$ strand haplotypes

$01111,00111,00011,00001,01011,01001,01101,00101,$

i.e. the $2^{3}=8$ strings $0\,x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}\,1$ with at most one

public_text.16:
On the + strand the two founders can be written as

$$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$$
and with a single, orientation fixed crossover a gamete which is made
from a pair $a,b$ is

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}\,,\qquad 0\le k\le 5 .$$

On the $F_{1}$ the two homologues are $A/B$ and, with the orientation
fixed on the $+$ strand,

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ haplotypes

$$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000  .$$

In particular every $F_{1}$ gamete and therefore every $F_{2}$
chromosome is monotone non-decreasing and contains no $1\to0$ descent.
Put $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.
Then

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}
$$

so that an $F_{3}$ gamete is the juxtaposition of a monotone left block
and a monotone right block.  Hence an $F_{3}$ gamete can contain at
most one $1\to0$ descent and the descent, if it is present, is forced
to be the junction $k\mid k+1$ of the crossover.  Up to the fixed
orientation a word with one descent is

$$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0 ,$$

and with $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1$

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}= \binom{n+1}{3}.$$

For $n=5$

$$N_{0}=n+1=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20 $$

so that on the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

different haploid sequences can be made in the gametes that form the
$F_{3}$.  For $n=5$

$$|{\cal H}_{3}|=6+20=26$$

distinct positive-strand haplotypes, the six monotone
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the $20$ one-descent
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes, e.g. $00101=001\;|\;01$, can be
present in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool.  The six $5$-bit words with $\ge2$
$1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., are first reached in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered diploid autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, attainable on the $+$ strand.  This is the usual
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count; with the two phases identified
it is the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ positive-strand words with $\le3$ runs,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes, quoted in the
phase-unrestricted literature. ∎

7.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are A=0⁵ and B=1⁵. With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis is the ordered splice

R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..5}, 0≤k≤5,

left block always from the first homologue. 

F₁: A/B gives on the + strand

H₁ = { R_k(A,B)=0^{k}1^{5-k} :0≤k≤5 } ,

the n+1=6 monotone 0*1* words

11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000.

Every F₂ chromosome is in H₁, hence monotone and has no 1→0 descent.

F₂→F₃: let a=0^{t₁}1^{5-t₁}, b=0^{t₂}1^{5-t₂}∈H₁ with t₁≤t₂. Then

R_k(a,b)= s_{t₂} for k≤t₁,
R_k(a,b)= s_{t₁} for k≥t₂,
R_k(a,b)=0^{t₁}1^{k-t₁}0^{t₂-k}1^{5-t₂} for t₁<k<t₂.

Hence an F₃ + strand gamete is monotone on the left of the cut and monotone on the right of the cut. The only 1→0 descent that can be created is the possible descent at the junction k|k+1. So the + strand F₃ set is the set of binary words of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent, i.e. words of the form

0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5.

N₀=n+1=6 monotone words. For a one-descent word b>0,c>0 put b'=b-1,c'=c-1. Then a+b'+c'+d=n-2, so

N₁(n)=# {a,b',c',d≥0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2}= C(n+1,3).

For n=5, N₁= C(6,3)=20, i.e. ∑_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20 words with the unique descent at position p. The 20 are the valley words 0^{t₁}1^{k-t₁}0^{t₂-k}1^{5-t₂} with 0≤t₁<k<t₂≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01.

Hence

|H₃⁺| = N₀+N₁ = n+1+ C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

distinct + strand haploid sequences attainable in the F₃ gamete pool. The six monotone words are already F₂; the 20 one-descent words are new in F₃. The two parental haplotypes 00000,11111 are included. The 2⁵=32 binary words are one descent short of saturation; the six words with ≥2 1→0 descents, e.g. 10101,01010, first appear in F₄.

The 22=2∑_{s=0}^{2}C(4,s) count is the ≤2-switch additive count and undercounts the junction-created descent. The stated strand asymmetry and “considering only the arbitrarily positive strand’’ removes the reciprocal phase double counting, giving the orientation-fixed 26 haplotype, 351 unordered diploid genotype limit, i.e. the n+1+ C(n+1,3) one-descent closure. ∎

i.e. the words with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent, the monotone case being
$b=0$ or $c=0$.  Conversely every binary word of length $5$ with at most
one $1\to0$ descent is of this form.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words.  For a one-descent word put $b'=b-1$,
$c'=c-1\ge0$, then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, $p(5-p)$ words with the descent at
$p$, $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$.  Hence on the fixed + orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct + strand haploid sequences are attainable in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool, $6$ monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and $20$ new valley
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The $2^{5}=32$ binary words are one
descent short of saturation; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $01010,10101$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered, $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$
autosomal genotypes.

The 30 $=2^{5}-2$ and 22 $=2\sum_{s=0}^{2}\binom{4}{s}$ counts quoted by
several colleagues arise when the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ products
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ are both admitted as distinct + strand
haplotypes, i.e. when the two phases of the $F_{1}$ heterozygote are kept
distinct.  With the stated one-way, strand-asymmetric recombination those
reciprocal products are the same physical event on the opposite strand
and are not scored on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand; the strict
orientation-fixed count is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=26$ one-descent set
above.  The 32 and 22 variants are over- and under-counts under the
given asymmetry. ∎

17.text:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$A=0^{5} ,\; B=1^{5}$ and put for a heterozygote $a/b$

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}\qquad0\le k\le5\;,$

the oriented one break product which is seen on the $+$ strand.
With the orientation fixed the F1 gamete pool is

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words

$11111,\;01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\;00000\;,$

i.e. the whole $F_{2}$ haploid pool.  In particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

Let $a=s_{t_{1}},\,b=s_{t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$, and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}}, &k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}}, &k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}}, &t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so that $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand haplotype can contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k\mid k+1$.  Up to the fixed
$0\to1$ orientation the attainable $+$ strand words are the binary
words of length $n$ with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent,

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

$N_{0}=n+1$ of them monotone, $w=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.

With $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the chosen
orientation

$\bigl|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}\bigr|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct $+$ strand haploid sequences can be made by two successive
oriented one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=5+1=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

i.e. the six $F_{2}$ monotone words
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$
and the twenty one-descent valley words

$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},\qquad0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5,$

e.g. $00101={\rm pref}_{3}(00111){\rm suff}_{2}(00001)$, etc.
In all

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$10101$ etc., are first reached in $F_{4}$.

On the unordered diploid level this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous
and $325$ heterozygous, the $6$ monotone haplotypes being the $F_{2}$
pool and the $20$ one-descent $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes being
new in $F_{3}$.  Up to the conventional reciprocal phase identification
this is the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ $+$/$-$ strand words with $\le3$
runs and $30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes. ∎

18.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains centred on the directed splice
$R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..n}$ on the arbitrarily chosen + strand with the two
founders $P_0=0^n$, $P_1=1^n$.
$F_1\to F_2$ gametes are the monotone $0\to1$ mosaics.
With formal ends $0\le k\le n$
${\cal H}_1=\{0^k1^{\,n-k}\}$, $|{\cal H}_1|=n+1=6$ for $n=5$,
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_2$ chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_2\to F_3$ gametes are $R_k(a,b)$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_1$.
For $a=0^{t_1}1^{n-t_1},b=0^{t_2}1^{n-t_2}$,
$t_1<t_2$,
$R_k(a,b)=0^{t_1}1^{k-t_1}0^{t_2-k}1^{n-t_2}$ for $t_1<k<t_2$,
otherwise $R_k$ is monotone. Hence an $F_3$ + strand word can be written
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=n$ and at most one $1\to0$ descent,
the descent if present being forced to the cut.  Up to the fixed
orientation the monotone words are $N_0=n+1$ and the one-descent words are

$N_1(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$,
$b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$.

For $n=5$ $N_0=6$, $N_1=\binom{6}{3}=20$,
$|{\cal H}_2|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$
distinct + strand haplotypes, the six $F_2$ monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and
the twenty valley $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  In diploid terms
$26^2=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_3$ autosomal
genotypes.  The $2^5=32$ binary words are one $1\to0$ descent short of
saturation; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$,
first appear in $F_4$.

The current round repeats this $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count.
Disagreement is the treatment of the endpoints and of the two reciprocal
phases.

* Formal ends $k=0,n$ are allowed in the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.
  With a strictly obligate internal cut $1\le k\le n-1$ the $F_1$ pool is
  the $n-1$ interior monotone strings $0^k1^{n-k}$, $k=1\ldots4$, and an
  $F_3$ + strand word must start with $0$ and end with $1$.  The attainable
  set is then the $2^{\,n-2}$ strings $0x_2\ldots x_{n-1}1$, i.e. $2^{3}=8$
  haplotypes
  $00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$
  and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes.  This is the
  $2^{n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit quoted by several colleagues.

* Allowing both reciprocal products $0^{k}1^{n-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{n-k}$ on
  the same nominal + strand gives the usual $2\sum_{s=0}^{g}\binom{n-1}{s}$
  switch count.  With $g=2$ meioses this is $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid words
  with $\le3$ switches, $01010$ and $10101$ being the only unreachable
  $4$-switch words.  The $22=2\sum_{s=0}^{2}\binom{4}{s}$ count is the
  $s\le2$ additive switch version often quoted as the $F_3$ limit.

The wording “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ and
“sufficient asymmetry … in only one orientation’’ points to the strict
interior, orientation-fixed model, i.e. the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid,
$36$ unordered diploid, limit.  The $26$ haploid, $351$ unordered diploid,
number is the conventional $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count obtained
once the formal $k=0,n$ terminal products are retained and the reciprocal
phase is identified with the opposite strand, which is the count most
colleagues in this round are reporting.  The 30/22/32 numbers correspond
to counting the two $F_1$ phases as distinct on the same strand or to
allowing no obligate crossover at the ends.  Unresolved is whether the
question expects the formal $k=0,n$ inclusion, $26$ haplotypes, or the
strict obligate interior interpretation, $8$ haplotypes.

reflection_text.3:

R_k(P0,P1)=P0[1:k]P1[k+1:5]=0^{k}1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5,

S1={s_t=0^{t}1^{5-t}}, |S1|=6.

With t1≤t2

* k≤t1 : s_{t2}
* k≥t2 : s_{t1}
* t1<k<t2 : 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2},

i.e. a word with at most one 1→0 descent. Conversely every binary word of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent can be written as a prefix of a s_t followed by a suffix of a s_u. Up to the fixed orientation these are the words

0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5, b>0⇒c>0,

the monotone words being b=0 or c=0 cases.

R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..5}, 0≤k≤5,

Founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$. 
With an obligate single, orientation-fixed crossover a gamete from $a/b$ is 
$R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..5}$, $0\le k\le5$, left block from the first homologue.

$F_{1}$ $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand
${\cal H}_{1}=R_k(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$, $|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$, no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$: let $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.
Then $R_k(a,b)$ is monotone on $1..k$ and on $k+1..5$. Hence an $F_{3}$ + strand
haplotype can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$.
For $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$

$R_k(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$,
$a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,\;c>0$, exactly one descent.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words.
With $b'=b-1,c'=c-1$, $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$, so
$N_{1}(n)=\binom{n+1}{3}$.
For $n=5$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, $p(5-p)$ words with descent at $p$,
$\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$.

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$ distinct + strand
haploid sequences in $F_{3}$, the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and the
20 one-descent valley words $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$. Two founders $00000,11111$
are included. Words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101,01010$, first appear
in $F_{4}$.

Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered, $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes.

Disagreements noted in round 1:
* 30 = $2^{5}-2$ haplotypes is the phase-unrestricted count obtained by
keeping both $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ gametes on the same
strand, i.e. $2\sum_{s\le3}\binom{4}{s}$. This double counts the reciprocal
product that the stated strand asymmetry forbids.
* 22 = $2\sum_{s\le2}\binom{4}{s}$ is the $s\le2$ additive switch count.
* 32 is saturation, $2^{5}$, unattainable with two oriented meioses.
* Strict interior $1\le k\le4$ gives $2^{n-2}=8$ + strand haplotypes
$0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$ with at most one descent, often quoted as the obligate
crossover limit.

Current belief: with the stated one-way orientation and counting only the
arbitrarily positive strand, the $F_{3}$ gamete pool is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$
one-descent set, $26$ haplotypes for $n=5$, the consensus of the oriented analysis.
The 26 vs 30 split is exactly the phase / reciprocal-product issue.

reflection_text.15:
The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are 
$P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$.  With the stated strand asymmetry a meiosis
from a pair $a,b$ is the ordered splice

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..5},\qquad 0\le k\le5$,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.  The
$F_{1}$ is $P_{0}/P_{1}$ so on the + strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$,

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

An $F_{3}$ gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$.  With
$a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ the left $k$ block and
right $5-k$ block of $R_{k}(a,b)$ are monotone, so $R_{k}(a,b)$ can have a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$.  For $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$

$R_{k}(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}
          =0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\;a+b+c+d=5,\;b>0,c>0,$

i.e. the words with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent, the monotone case being
$b=0$ or $c=0$.  Conversely every binary word of length $5$ with at most
one $1\to0$ descent is of this form.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words.  For a one-descent word put $b'=b-1$,
$c'=c-1\ge0$, then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, $p(5-p)$ words with the descent at
$p$, $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$.  Hence on the fixed + orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct + strand haploid sequences are attainable in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool, $6$ monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and $20$ new valley
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The $2^{5}=32$ binary words are one
descent short of saturation; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $01010,10101$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered, $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$
autosomal genotypes.

The 30 $=2^{5}-2$ and 22 $=2\sum_{s=0}^{2}\binom{4}{s}$ counts quoted by
several colleagues arise when the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ products
$0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ are both admitted as distinct + strand
haplotypes, i.e. when the two phases of the $F_{1}$ heterozygote are kept
distinct.  With the stated one-way, strand-asymmetric recombination those
reciprocal products are the same physical event on the opposite strand
and are not scored on the arbitrarily chosen positive strand; the strict
orientation-fixed count is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=26$ one-descent set
above.  The 32 and 22 variants are over- and under-counts under the
given asymmetry. ∎
reflection_text.17:
On the $+$ strand write the two founders as

$A=0^{5} ,\; B=1^{5}$ and put for a heterozygote $a/b$

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}\qquad0\le k\le5\;,$

the oriented one break product which is seen on the $+$ strand.
With the orientation fixed the F1 gamete pool is

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{s_{k}=0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words

$11111,\;01111,\;00111,\;00011,\;00001,\;00000\;,$

i.e. the whole $F_{2}$ haploid pool.  In particular every $F_{2}$
chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

Let $a=s_{t_{1}},\,b=s_{t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$, and let the
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ break be $k$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}}, &k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}}, &k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}}, &t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so that $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand haplotype can contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k\mid k+1$.  Up to the fixed
$0\to1$ orientation the attainable $+$ strand words are the binary
words of length $n$ with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent,

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

$N_{0}=n+1$ of them monotone, $w=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.

With $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the chosen
orientation

$\bigl|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}\bigr|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct $+$ strand haploid sequences can be made by two successive
oriented one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=5+1=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

i.e. the six $F_{2}$ monotone words
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$
and the twenty one-descent valley words

$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},\qquad0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5,$

e.g. $00101={\rm pref}_{3}(00111){\rm suff}_{2}(00001)$, etc.
In all

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$10101$ etc., are first reached in $F_{4}$.

On the unordered diploid level this is $26^{2}=676$ ordered and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous
and $325$ heterozygous, the $6$ monotone haplotypes being the $F_{2}$
pool and the $20$ one-descent $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes being
new in $F_{3}$.  Up to the conventional reciprocal phase identification
this is the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ $+$/$-$ strand words with $\le3$
runs and $30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid genotypes. ∎
reflection_text.18:
The discussion remains centred on the directed splice
$R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..n}$ on the arbitrarily chosen + strand with the two
founders $P_0=0^n$, $P_1=1^n$.
$F_1\to F_2$ gametes are the monotone $0\to1$ mosaics.
With formal ends $0\le k\le n$
${\cal H}_1=\{0^k1^{\,n-k}\}$, $|{\cal H}_1|=n+1=6$ for $n=5$,
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
Every $F_2$ chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_2\to F_3$ gametes are $R_k(a,b)$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_1$.
For $a=0^{t_1}1^{n-t_1},b=0^{t_2}1^{n-t_2}$,
$t_1<t_2$,
$R_k(a,b)=0^{t_1}1^{k-t_1}0^{t_2-k}1^{n-t_2}$ for $t_1<k<t_2$,
otherwise $R_k$ is monotone. Hence an $F_3$ + strand word can be written
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=n$ and at most one $1\to0$ descent,
the descent if present being forced to the cut.  Up to the fixed
orientation the monotone words are $N_0=n+1$ and the one-descent words are

$N_1(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$,
$b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$.

For $n=5$ $N_0=6$, $N_1=\binom{6}{3}=20$,
$|{\cal H}_2|=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$
distinct + strand haplotypes, the six $F_2$ monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and
the twenty valley $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  In diploid terms
$26^2=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_3$ autosomal
genotypes.  The $2^5=32$ binary words are one $1\to0$ descent short of
saturation; the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$,
first appear in $F_4$.

The current round repeats this $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count.
Disagreement is the treatment of the endpoints and of the two reciprocal
phases.

* Formal ends $k=0,n$ are allowed in the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ count.
  With a strictly obligate internal cut $1\le k\le n-1$ the $F_1$ pool is
  the $n-1$ interior monotone strings $0^k1^{n-k}$, $k=1\ldots4$, and an
  $F_3$ + strand word must start with $0$ and end with $1$.  The attainable
  set is then the $2^{\,n-2}$ strings $0x_2\ldots x_{n-1}1$, i.e. $2^{3}=8$
  haplotypes
  $00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$
  and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes.  This is the
  $2^{n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit quoted by several colleagues.

* Allowing both reciprocal products $0^{k}1^{n-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{n-k}$ on
  the same nominal + strand gives the usual $2\sum_{s=0}^{g}\binom{n-1}{s}$
  switch count.  With $g=2$ meioses this is $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid words
  with $\le3$ switches, $01010$ and $10101$ being the only unreachable
  $4$-switch words.  The $22=2\sum_{s=0}^{2}\binom{4}{s}$ count is the
  $s\le2$ additive switch version often quoted as the $F_3$ limit.

The wording “exactly one locus per generation for every gamete’’ and
“sufficient asymmetry … in only one orientation’’ points to the strict
interior, orientation-fixed model, i.e. the $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid,
$36$ unordered diploid, limit.  The $26$ haploid, $351$ unordered diploid,
number is the conventional $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent count obtained
once the formal $k=0,n$ terminal products are retained and the reciprocal
phase is identified with the opposite strand, which is the count most
colleagues in this round are reporting.  The 30/22/32 numbers correspond
to counting the two $F_1$ phases as distinct on the same strand or to
allowing no obligate crossover at the ends.  Unresolved is whether the
question expects the formal $k=0,n$ inclusion, $26$ haplotypes, or the
strict obligate interior interpretation, $8$ haplotypes.

1.text:
On the fixed orientation write the parents on the $+$ strand as
$A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and put for a directed one break

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad0\le k\le5, $$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal product is on the opposite strand and is not scored on
the $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$,

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

i.e. every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and contains no
$1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the same meioses read on
the complementary strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to
the fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

with $b>0,c>0$ for the non-monotone case.  With $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$

$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$,

so that

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent and

$N_{0}(n)=n+1$

words are monotone.  Hence on the chosen $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ 

distinct haploid sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$,

the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101$, with the two founders $00000$ and $11111$ included.
The six $2^{5}$ words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., are
first reachable in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ oriented haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the conventional $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent
closure on the fixed $+$ strand.  Allowing the two reciprocal $F_{1}$
phases to be counted as distinct $+$ strand haplotypes this is the
usual $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count. ∎

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the asymmetry is decisive. Write the founders on that strand as A = 00000, B = 11111 and the directed one-break gamete from a pair a,b as

R_k(a,b)= a_{1..k} b_{k+1..5},   0≤k≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal product R_k(b,a) is the same physical recombinant seen on the opposite strand and is not counted on the chosen + strand.

F1. A/B gives on +

H1 = R_k(A,B)= {0^k1^{5-k} : 0≤k≤5}
= 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,

the n+1 =6 monotone 0*1* words. Every F2 chromosome is a/b with a,b∈H1 and therefore monotone, with no 1→0 descent.

F2→F3. Let a=0^{t1}1^{5-t1}, b=0^{t2}1^{5-t2}∈H1, t1≤t2. Then

R_k(a,b)= s_{t2} for k≤t1,
        = s_{t1} for k≥t2,
        = 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} for t1<k<t2.

The left k-mer and the right 5-k-mer are each monotone. Hence an F3 + strand gamete can contain a 1→0 descent only at the junction k|k+1, and at most once. Up to the fixed orientation

w = 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5,

with b>0,c>0 for the non-monotone case. Put b'=b-1,c'=c-1≥0, then a+b'+c'+d=3 and

N1(n)= #{a+b'+c'+d=n-2}= C(n+1,3).

With N0=n+1 monotone words the + strand haplotype closure after two directed obligate cross-overs is

|H3| = N0+N1 = n+1+ C(n+1,3).

For n=5

N0=6, N1= C(6,3)=20, |H3|=6+20=26.

The six monotone F2 words are 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. The 20 new F3 valley words are 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} with 0≤t1<k<t2≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01, 01011, 01101, etc. They are exactly the ≤1 1→0 descent words.

Words with ≥2 1→0 descents such as 10101, 01010, 10100, 10010 cannot be written as a[1:k]b[k+1:5] with a,b monotone 0^p1^{5-p}. They need a second descent and first appear in F4. The 2^5=32 binary words are one descent short of saturation.

In diploid terms this is 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomal genotypes.

The 30=2^5-2 figure is the phase-unrestricted count obtained by admitting both 0^k1^{5-k} and 1^k0^{5-k} as distinct + strand F1 haplotypes, i.e. by counting the reciprocal product of the first meiosis on the same arbitrarily chosen strand. With the stated strand asymmetry that reciprocal product belongs to the opposite strand and must not be double counted on the fixed + strand. Restricted to the single directed orientation the attainable + strand set is the 26 one-descent haplotypes above.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the asymmetry is decisive.  
Write the two inbred founders on that strand as $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and let the obligatory oriented gamete from a pair $a,b$ be

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal product $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the opposite strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

$F_{1}$.  The $F_{1}$ heterozygote is $A/B$ so on the + strand

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

Those are the $F_{1}$ gametes and hence the whole $F_{2}$ haploid pool. In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ and contains no $1\to0$ descent. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products of the same $F_{1}$ meiosis; with a strictly one-way crossover they belong to the opposite strand and are not distinct + strand haplotypes.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$. An $F_{3}$ gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$.  For $t_{1}\le t_{2}$

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$$

so the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are each monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  The only $1\to0$ descent that can be created in the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the possible descent at the junction $k|k+1$, and it can occur at most once.

Hence every + strand $F_{3}$ haplotype is $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$.  The zero-descent case is the $F_{2}$ pool

$N_{0}=n+1=6$,

$0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  For exactly one descent $b>0,c>0$, put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$. Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}.$$

For $n=5$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, i.e. $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$ valley words $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$.

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$$

distinct + strand haploid sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome, the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the twenty one-descent $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The six binary words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$, are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

The $2^{5}-2=30$ count re-introduces the $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products as distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. it counts the reciprocal phase of the first meiosis on the same arbitrarily chosen strand.  With sufficient asymmetry in only one orientation that reciprocal product is not present on the chosen + strand; it is the same meiosis seen on the complementary strand.  Removing that double counting the $F_{1}$ pool is the six monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ words, not the ten two-phase set, and the second oriented splice can give at most one $1\to0$ descent.  That is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed limit, $6+20=26$ haploid + strand sequences in $F_{3}$, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid autosomal genotypes. ∎

10.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand write the two founders

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$,

and with the strand asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the $+$
strand from a heterozygote $a/b$ is the ordered mosaic

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal $b_{1\ldots k}a_{k+1\ldots5}$ is the same meiosis read on
the opposite strand and is not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

so every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$ and $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are both monotone.
A $+$ strand $F_{3}$ gamete can therefore contain a $1\to0$ descent
only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the fixed
orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,\;b,c\ge0$,

is the whole attainable set, i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with
$\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.
With exactly one descent $b>0,\;c>0$ put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  For $n=5$

$N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)$

one-descent valley words $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$t_{1}<k<t_{2}$, e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.

Hence on the fixed $+$ orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome, the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ haplotypes and the
twenty one-descent $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The two founders
$00000,11111$ are included and the six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$
descents, e.g. $10101,01010$, are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes pair to $26^{2}=676$ ordered
maternal$\times$paternal autosomes and $\,26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered

This is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed
closure.  Allowing the reciprocal $F_{1}$ phase on the same strand the
familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ phased haplotypes, $465$ unordered diploid
genotypes, is recovered. ∎

haploid + strand sequences, the six $F_{2}$ monotone

7.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand the directed gamete made from a
pair $a,b$ is

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad 0\le k\le5,
$$

the left block being taken from the first homologue.  On the $+$ strand

$$
P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5},
$$

and

$$
{\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\;:\;0\le k\le5\}
$$

is the $F_{1}\to F_{2}$ gamete pool.  Up to the fixed orientation this is
the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$$
11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,
$$

the $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ reciprocal products being the same meioses on the
opposite strand.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is therefore monotone and
contains no $1\to0$ descent.

{\cal H}_{1}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}}, & k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}}, & k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}, & t_{1}<k<t_{2},
\end{cases}
$$

so the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are each monotone.
Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at
the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the fixed orientation

$$
w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,
$$

with the zero–descent monotone case $c=0$ and the one–descent case
$b>0,\;c>0$.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.
For a one–descent word put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}
       =\binom{n+1}{3}.
$$

For $n=5$

$$
N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,
$$

i.e. $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$ valley words
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, etc.

Hence on the fixed $+$ orientation

$$
|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26
$$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can be produced by two successive
oriented one-break meioses.  The six monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ words are

$1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101,01010$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal realisations and
$26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous
and $325$ heterozygous.  This is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent,
orientation-fixed closure.  Allowing the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ phases
to be counted as distinct on the same strand the familiar
$2^{5}-2=30$ haplotype, $465$ unordered diploid genotype count is
recovered. ∎
