Let $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}
\in{\cal H}_{1}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be
$k$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}}, &k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}}, &k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  An $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can therefore contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most one such
descent can be created.  Up to the fixed orientation the attainable
$+$ strand words are

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.  The
$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$ pool.  A
word with exactly one $1\to0$ descent can be written
$0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $b>0,c>0$.  Putting $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$,

$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$,

so that

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct haploid sequences can be made by two successive oriented
one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,$

the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the 20 one-descent valley haplotypes

$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},\qquad0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101,01011,01101\ldots$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$ different $+$ strand haplotypes in the
$F_{3}$ gamete pool.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$10101$, $01010$, etc., are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the 26 haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$\displaystyle \frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, 26 homozygous and 325
heterozygous, on the chosen strand.  This is the usual
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent closure, $6+20=26$ $+$ strand
haplotypes, which is the $2^{5}-2=30$ phase-unrestricted $+$/$-$ count
when the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ products $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and
$1^{k}0^{5-k}$ are identified.  With a strictly interior obligate cut
$1\le k\le4$ the terminal $k=0,5$ products are removed and the
$+$ strand $0\!-\!1$ fixed set is $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haplotypes,
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, the textbook
obligate-crossover limit. ∎

18.text:
On the $+$ strand put $P_{0}=0^{5}$ and $P_{1}=1^{5}$ and write the
directed one break product

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}\qquad0\le k\le5,
$$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
Up to the chosen orientation

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}_{0\le k\le5}$,

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$,

is the $F_{1}$ gamete pool and hence the $F_{2}$ haploid pool.  An
$F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and an
$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ gamete is again $R_{k}(a,b)$.  With
$a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$,

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=\left\{\begin{array}{ll}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{array}\right.
$$

so that $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$–strand word can contain a $1\to0$
descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and it can be written in the
canonical form

$$
w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,
$$

the monotone case being $c=0$.  With $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$ for the
one–descent case

$$
a+b'+c'+d=5-2
$$

so that

$$
N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}
$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  The zero-descent monotone
set is $N_{0}(n)=n+1$.  Hence on the fixed orientation

$$
|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}
$$

$+$–strand haploid types can be made by two successive directed
one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$$
N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20,
$$

i.e. the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$ together with the $20$
valley haplotypes $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.
In particular

$$
|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26
$$

different $+$–strand chromosomes can segregate in the $F_{3}$ gamete
pool.  The $2^{5}=32$ binary words are one descent short of saturation;
the six words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$, $01010$, etc.,
first appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$
\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351
$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, on the chosen $+$ strand.  This is the usual
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed closure.  Removing
the formal terminal cuts $k=0,5$ and insisting on a strictly interior
obligate break $1\le k\le4$, the $+$–strand words must start $0$ and
end $1$,

$$
0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1,
$$

i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haploid types
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, the $8\times9/2=36$
unordered diploid, $8^{2}=64$ ordered diploid, obligate-crossover limit
often quoted as the $2^{\,n-2}$ limit.  The $26$–haplotype count above
is the $k=0,5$–inclusive $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ form. ∎

public_text.1:
On the fixed orientation write the parents on the $+$ strand as
$A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and put for a directed one break

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad0\le k\le5, $$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
The reciprocal product is on the opposite strand and is not scored on
the $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$,

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ haplotypes

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

i.e. every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and contains no
$1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the same meioses read on
the complementary strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Let $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)$ is monotone on $1\ldots k$ and monotone on
$k+1\ldots5$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to
the fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

with $b>0,c>0$ for the non-monotone case.  With $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$

$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$,

so that

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent and

$N_{0}(n)=n+1$

words are monotone.  Hence on the chosen $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ 

distinct haploid sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$,

the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101$, with the two founders $00000$ and $11111$ included.

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the conventional $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent
closure on the fixed $+$ strand.  Allowing the two reciprocal $F_{1}$
phases to be counted as distinct $+$ strand haplotypes this is the
usual $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count. ∎
public_text.9:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the asymmetry is decisive. Write the founders on that strand as A = 00000, B = 11111 and the directed one-break gamete from a pair a,b as

R_k(a,b)= a_{1..k} b_{k+1..5},   0≤k≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal product R_k(b,a) is the same physical recombinant seen on the opposite strand and is not counted on the chosen + strand.

F1. A/B gives on +

H1 = R_k(A,B)= {0^k1^{5-k} : 0≤k≤5}
= 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,

the n+1 =6 monotone 0*1* words. Every F2 chromosome is a/b with a,b∈H1 and therefore monotone, with no 1→0 descent.

F2→F3. Let a=0^{t1}1^{5-t1}, b=0^{t2}1^{5-t2}∈H1, t1≤t2. Then

R_k(a,b)= s_{t2} for k≤t1,
        = s_{t1} for k≥t2,
        = 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} for t1<k<t2.

The left k-mer and the right 5-k-mer are each monotone. Hence an F3 + strand gamete can contain a 1→0 descent only at the junction k|k+1, and at most once. Up to the fixed orientation

w = 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5,

with b>0,c>0 for the non-monotone case. Put b'=b-1,c'=c-1≥0, then a+b'+c'+d=3 and

N1(n)= #{a+b'+c'+d=n-2}= C(n+1,3).

With N0=n+1 monotone words the + strand haplotype closure after two directed obligate cross-overs is

|H3| = N0+N1 = n+1+ C(n+1,3).

For n=5

N0=6, N1= C(6,3)=20, |H3|=6+20=26.

The six monotone F2 words are 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. The 20 new F3 valley words are 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} with 0≤t1<k<t2≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01, 01011, 01101, etc. They are exactly the ≤1 1→0 descent words.

Words with ≥2 1→0 descents such as 10101, 01010, 10100, 10010 cannot be written as a[1:k]b[k+1:5] with a,b monotone 0^p1^{5-p}. They need a second descent and first appear in F4. The 2^5=32 binary words are one descent short of saturation.

In diploid terms this is 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomal genotypes.

The 30=2^5-2 figure is the phase-unrestricted count obtained by admitting both 0^k1^{5-k} and 1^k0^{5-k} as distinct + strand F1 haplotypes, i.e. by counting the reciprocal product of the first meiosis on the same arbitrarily chosen strand. With the stated strand asymmetry that reciprocal product belongs to the opposite strand and must not be double counted on the fixed + strand. Restricted to the single directed orientation the attainable + strand set is the 26 one-descent haplotypes above.
public_text.2:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the asymmetry is decisive.  
Write the two inbred founders on that strand as $A=0^{5}$ and $B=1^{5}$ and let the obligatory oriented gamete from a pair $a,b$ be

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal product $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the opposite strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

$F_{1}$.  The $F_{1}$ heterozygote is $A/B$ so on the + strand

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0\to1$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

Those are the $F_{1}$ gametes and hence the whole $F_{2}$ haploid pool. In particular every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ and contains no $1\to0$ descent. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products of the same $F_{1}$ meiosis; with a strictly one-way crossover they belong to the opposite strand and are not distinct + strand haplotypes.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  An $F_{2}$ individual is $a/b$ with $a,b\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$. An $F_{3}$ gamete is $R_{k}(a,b)$.  For $t_{1}\le t_{2}$

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$$

so the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are each monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  The only $1\to0$ descent that can be created in the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the possible descent at the junction $k|k+1$, and it can occur at most once.

Hence every + strand $F_{3}$ haplotype is $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ with $a+b+c+d=5$.  The zero-descent case is the $F_{2}$ pool

$N_{0}=n+1=6$,

$0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  For exactly one descent $b>0,c>0$, put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$. Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}.$$

For $n=5$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, i.e. $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4=20$ valley words $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$.

Thus on the fixed orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$$

distinct + strand haploid sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome, the six monotone $F_{2}$ haplotypes and the twenty one-descent $0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$ haplotypes.  The six binary words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$, are first reachable in $F_{4}$.

The $2^{5}-2=30$ count re-introduces the $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products as distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. it counts the reciprocal phase of the first meiosis on the same arbitrarily chosen strand.  With sufficient asymmetry in only one orientation that reciprocal product is not present on the chosen + strand; it is the same meiosis seen on the complementary strand.  Removing that double counting the $F_{1}$ pool is the six monotone $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ words, not the ten two-phase set, and the second oriented splice can give at most one $1\to0$ descent.  That is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed limit, $6+20=26$ haploid + strand sequences in $F_{3}$, $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered diploid autosomal genotypes. ∎

\end{cases}

18.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are
$P_{0}=0^{5},\,P_{1}=1^{5}$ and with the stated strand asymmetry the gamete
seen on the + strand from a heterozygote $a/b$ is the ordered splice
$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}$.
The reciprocal $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis on the opposite
strand.

$F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$.  $P_{0}/P_{1}$ gives on the + strand
${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}$.  With formal ends
$0\le k\le5$ this is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone
and contains no $1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal
products on the opposite strand.

$F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$.  For $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$,

$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{2}}$ for $k\le t_{1}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{1}}$ for $k\ge t_{2}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ for $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$.

Hence the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are both monotone.
An $F_{3}$ + strand gamete can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction
$k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the fixed orientation
$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\;a+b+c+d=5$.
$N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words.  With $b>0,c>0$, $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$,
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$, so

$N_{1}(n)=\binom{n+1}{3}$ words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.

With formal ends $k=0,n$ inclusive

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}.$

For $n=5$, $N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$ distinct + strand haploid sequences,
the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and the twenty
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ valley words.
Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered, $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$
autosomal genotypes.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $10101,01010$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

This is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation fixed closure
being quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,18 in this round.
Counting the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ phases as distinct on the same formal
strand gives the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid count, i.e. all words with $\le3$
switches.

Strict obligate-crossover reading.  The statement “exactly one locus per
generation for every gamete’’ is an obligate internal cut,
$1\le k\le n-1$.  Then ${\cal H}_{1}$ is the $n-1=4$ interior monotone
words $0^{k}1^{5-k}$, $k=1\!:\!4$, and every $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ product
starts $0$ and ends $1$,

$w=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,

so $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haploid + strand types
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes.
This is the $2^{\,n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit noted by Colleague 4
and in the earlier discussion.

The current round consensus is the formal-ends inclusive $26$ haploid
$/$ $351$ unordered diploid count.  The unresolved tension is whether the
problem intends the formal $k=0,n$ terminal products to be kept, giving
$26$, or the strict obligate interior $1\le k\le4$ interpretation,
giving $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid $/$ $36$ unordered diploid.
The $22$, $30$, $32$ numbers correspond to counting the two reciprocal
$F_{1}$ phases as distinct on the + strand or to additive switch
counting.

reflection_text.1:
The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are A=00000, B=11111. With strand-asymmetric obligate recombination the + strand product of a heterozygote a/b is the ordered splice R_k(a,b)=a[1:k]b[k+1:5], 0≤k≤5, left block from first homologue, right block from second. The reciprocal 1^k0^{5-k} product is on the opposite strand and is not counted on the fixed + strand.

F1→F2: R_k(A,B)=0^k1^{5-k}, 0≤k≤5. Hence H1 = {0^k1^{5-k}} , |H1|=n+1=6, the monotone 0*1* F2 haplotype pool. Every F2 chromosome is monotone, no 1→0 descent.

F2→F3: a=s_{t1}=0^{t1}1^{5-t1}, b=s_{t2}=0^{t2}1^{5-t2}∈H1. Then R_k(a,b)=a_{1:k}b_{k+1:5} is monotone on 1..k and monotone on k+1..5. Hence an + strand F3 gamete can contain a 1→0 descent only at the junction k. Up to trivial k≤t1,k≥t2 the non-monotone forms are 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2}=0^a1^b0^c1^d, a+b+c+d=5,b>0,c>0, exactly one 1→0 descent. With b'=b-1,c'=c-1≥0, a+b'+c'+d=3. Hence N1(n)=C(n+1,3), N0=n+1.

For n=5: N0=6, N1=C(6,3)=20. The 20 one-descent words are 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} with 0≤t1<k<t2≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01. The six monotone words are already present in F2.

Thus on the strictly oriented + strand |H3|+ = n+1+C(n+1,3)=6+20=26 distinct haploid 5-bit sequences, the two founders included. The 32 binary words are one descent short of saturation; the six words with ≥2 1→0 descents, 10101,01010 etc., first appear in F4.

Diploid: 26^2=676 ordered maternal×paternal, 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomal genotypes, 26 homozygous, 325 heterozygous.

Current round consensus is the 26/351 one-descent orientation-fixed count. Disagreements are purely counting convention:

* Strictly oriented + strand as stated → 26 haploid, 351 unordered diploid. This is the n+1+C(n+1,3) one-descent count repeated by colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,18,2,3,6,7,8,9 in round 2.
* If the two reciprocal F1 products 0^k1^{5-k} and 1^k0^{5-k} are both admitted as distinct + strand haplotypes, the F1 pool is 10 and the second splice gives all words with ≤3 switches: 2∑_{s=0}^{3}C(4,s)=30=2^5-2 haploid, 465 unordered diploid, 900 ordered. This is the familiar 30/465 number.
* Additive switch counting s≤2 gives 2[ C(4,0)+C(4,1)+C(4,2)]=22 haploid.
* With strictly interior obligate break 1≤k≤4 and fixed maternal→paternal order the + strand set is the 0xxx1 class 2^{n-2}=8 haploid, 36 unordered diploid.

Unresolved notation: whether k=0,5 trivial crossovers are counted – the 26 count includes them as parental recovery; the interior-only limit is 8. The question asks for “unique sequences of this autosome”; the consensus haploid + strand answer is 26, diploid unordered 351. If diploid genotypes are required the numbers are 676 ordered / 351 unordered.
reflection_text.6:
The two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are A=0^5, B=1^5. With the stated strand asymmetry the oriented gamete from a/b is R_k(a,b)=a_{1..k}b_{k+1..5}, 0≤k≤5, left block from the first homologue only. The reciprocal product is on the opposite strand and is not counted on the chosen + strand.

F1→F2. A/B gives on + H1 = R_k(A,B) = {0^k1^{5-k}:0≤k≤5} = 0*1* monotone words, |H1|=n+1=6. These are 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111. Every F2 chromosome is monotone and contains no 1→0 descent. The 1^k0^{5-k} words are the same meioses read on the complementary strand.

F2→F3. Let a=0^{t1}1^{5-t1}, b=0^{t2}1^{5-t2}∈H1, t1≤t2. 
R_k(a,b)= s_{t2} if k≤t1, s_{t1} if k≥t2, 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} if t1<k<t2.
Hence R_k(a,b) is monotone on 1..k and monotone on k+1..5. The only 1→0 descent that can appear is at the junction k|k+1, at most once.

Thus F3 + strand haplotypes are binary words of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent, i.e. 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}, a+b+c+d=5.

N0=n+1 monotone zero-descent words.
A word with exactly one descent is 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d} with b>0,c>0. Put b'=b-1,c'=c-1≥0. Then a+b'+c'+d=n-2. Number = C(n+1,3).
For n=5, N0=6, N1=C(6,3)=20, sum p(5-p)=1·4+2·3+3·2+4·1=20.
|H3^+|=N0+N1=n+1+C(n+1,3)=6+20=26 distinct + strand haploid sequences. The six monotone words are the F2 set; the 20 valley words 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2}, t1<k<t2, are new in F3. Words needing ≥2 1→0 descents, e.g. 10101,01010, first appear in F4. 2^5=32 is one descent short of saturation.

Diploid: 26^2=676 ordered maternal×paternal, 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomal genotypes, 26 homozygous + 325 heterozygous.

Disagreements noted:
* 30=2^5-2 haplotypes, 465 unordered diploid, is the count obtained when both reciprocal F1 products 0^k1^{5-k} and 1^k0^{5-k} are admitted on the same + strand, i.e. counting the opposite orientation as distinct. This is the phase-unrestricted count. With the stated single-orientation asymmetry this double counts the reciprocal product.
* 22 = 2[ C(4,0)+C(4,1)+C(4,2)] is the ≤2 switch additive count; it undercounts the junction-created descent.
* 32 is the formal 2^5 upper bound ignoring the one-crossover-per-generation constraint.

Current belief remains under the explicitly stated one orientation only and + strand only, the attainable F3 haploid diversity is the one-descent set n+1+C(n+1,3)=26 haplotypes, 351 unordered diploid genotypes. If the question is phrased as haploid sequences, 26; if diploid genotypes are required, 351 unordered / 676 ordered. The 30/465 count is the conventional phase-unrestricted version. ∎

* k≤t1 : s_{t2}
* k≥t2 : s_{t1}
* t1<k<t2 : 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2},

i.e. a word with at most one 1→0 descent. Conversely every binary word of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent can be written as a prefix of a s_t followed by a suffix of a s_u.

In diploid terms 26^2=676 ordered and 26·27/2=351 unordered F3 autosomal genotypes.

The repeated disagreement in the literature is the phase double-count. If the two reciprocal F1 orientations 0^{k}1^{5-k} and 1^{k}0^{5-k} are both kept in S1 the second recombination gives all words with ≤3 switches, i.e. all 32 binary words except 01010 and 10101, 30=2^5-2 haplotypes, 465 unordered diploid genotypes. Strictly interior obligate break 1≤k≤4 gives 2^{n-2}=8 positive-strand haplotypes 0xxx1, 36 unordered diploid.

Under the problem statement – obligate one cut per gamete, fixed recombination orientation and counting only the arbitrarily chosen + strand – the coherent fixed-orientation set is the 26 one-descent haplotypes, 6 monotone plus 20 valley, the textbook n+1+C(n+1,3) result. Current round consensus from Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,15,16,17,18 and 2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 is 26 haploid, 351 unordered diploid, with the 30=2^5-2 count noted as the two-phase version. reflection_text.18:
The two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are
$P_{0}=0^{5},\,P_{1}=1^{5}$ and with the stated strand asymmetry the gamete
seen on the + strand from a heterozygote $a/b$ is the ordered splice
$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}$.
The reciprocal $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis on the opposite
strand.

$F_{1}\!\to\!F_{2}$.  $P_{0}/P_{1}$ gives on the + strand
${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}\}$.  With formal ends
$0\le k\le5$ this is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone
and contains no $1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal
products on the opposite strand.

$F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$.  For $a=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$,

$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{2}}$ for $k\le t_{1}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{1}}$ for $k\ge t_{2}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ for $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$.

Hence the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are both monotone.
An $F_{3}$ + strand gamete can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction
$k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the fixed orientation
$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\;a+b+c+d=5$.
$N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words.  With $b>0,c>0$, $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$,
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$, so

$N_{1}(n)=\binom{n+1}{3}$ words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.

With formal ends $k=0,n$ inclusive

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}.$

For $n=5$, $N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$ distinct + strand haploid sequences,
the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and the twenty
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ valley words.
Diploid: $26^{2}=676$ ordered, $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$
autosomal genotypes.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
e.g. $10101,01010$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

This is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation fixed closure
being quoted by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,18 in this round.
Counting the two reciprocal $F_{1}$ phases as distinct on the same formal
strand gives the familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid,
$30\cdot31/2=465$ unordered diploid count, i.e. all words with $\le3$
switches.

Strict obligate-crossover reading.  The statement “exactly one locus per
generation for every gamete’’ is an obligate internal cut,
$1\le k\le n-1$.  Then ${\cal H}_{1}$ is the $n-1=4$ interior monotone
words $0^{k}1^{5-k}$, $k=1\!:\!4$, and every $F_{2}\!\to\!F_{3}$ product
starts $0$ and ends $1$,

$w=0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,

so $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haploid + strand types
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes.
This is the $2^{\,n-2}$ obligate-crossover limit noted by Colleague 4
and in the earlier discussion.

The current round consensus is the formal-ends inclusive $26$ haploid
$/$ $351$ unordered diploid count.  The unresolved tension is whether the
problem intends the formal $k=0,n$ terminal products to be kept, giving
$26$, or the strict obligate interior $1\le k\le4$ interpretation,
giving $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid $/$ $36$ unordered diploid.
The $22$, $30$, $32$ numbers correspond to counting the two reciprocal
$F_{1}$ phases as distinct on the + strand or to additive switch
counting.

3.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put the two founders

$P_{0}=0^{5}=00000,\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}=11111$

and with the stated one way asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the +
strand from an ordered heterozygote $a/b$ is

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.  The
reciprocal $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the $-$
strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$ .  $A/B$ gives on the + strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

$s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ and
is monotone, no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$ .  Let $a=s_{t_{1}},b=s_{t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$ with
$t_{1}\le t_{2}$.

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so the left $k$–block and the right $5-k$–block are each monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$.  An $F_{3}$ + strand gamete can therefore contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the
fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

$\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone zero-descent words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$
pool.  For a one-descent word $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed + orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)$,

the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$ and the twenty one-descent valley
haplotypes $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101,01011,01101$, etc.  The two founders are included and the
six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101,01010$ etc., first
appear in $F_{4}$.

segregate in the $F_{3}$ gamete pool, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent
closure on the fixed orientation.  In diploid terms this is
$26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal
genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$ heterozygous.

The familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count is
recovered if the reciprocal $F_{1}$ products $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ are admitted
as distinct + strand haplotypes, i.e. on the phase-unrestricted
strand.  With the stated sufficient asymmetry and the restriction to
the arbitrarily chosen positive strand the strict attainable set is the
26 one-descent haplotypes above. ∎

With the orientation fixed the $F_{1}$ pool is the six monotone $s_{k}$ and the second directed splice gives at most one $1\to0$ descent, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=26$ one-descent closure on the chosen + strand.

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put the two inbred founders

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$

and with the one way asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the $+$ 
strand from a heterozygote $a/b$ is the ordered mosaic

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.  The
reciprocal $b_{1\ldots k}a_{k+1\ldots5}$ is the same meiosis read on the
$-$ strand and is not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.

Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and contains no
$1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products
on the opposite strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Put $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}}, & k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}}, & k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}}, & t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so the left $k$–block and the right $5-k$–block are both monotone.
An $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can therefore contain a $1\to0$ descent
only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  In canonical form

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

with at most one $1\to0$ descent.  The zero-descent monotone set is

$N_{0}=n+1=6$,

$0^{t}1^{5-t}$.

For a non monotone word $b>0,c>0$.  Put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)$,

i.e. the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.  The two founders are
included.  The six $2^{5}$ words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$10101$ etc., first require a second oriented splice and first appear
in $F_{4}$.

Hence

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$

distinct $+$ strand haploid sequences can be segregating in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  On the orientation fixed $+$ strand this is the
$n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent closure.  In diploid terms the 26
haplotypes pair to

$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal autosomes and

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous.

Allowing the reciprocal $F_{1}$ phase $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ to be counted as a
distinct $+$ strand haplotype the familiar phase-unrestricted
$2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count is recovered.  With
a strictly interior obligate cut $1\le k\le4$ the $k=0,5$ trivial
classes are removed and the $+$ strand $0\!-\!1$ fixed set is the
textbook $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid, $36$ unordered diploid, obligate-
crossover limit. ∎

18.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen + strand write the two inbred founders as

$P_{0}=0^{5},\qquad P_{1}=1^{5}$

and with the one way asymmetry let the gamete that is seen on the +
strand from a heterozygote $a/b$ be the ordered splice

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad 0\le k\le 5, $$

the left block being taken from the first homologue and the right block
from the second.  The reciprocal $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical
meiosis seen on the $-$ strand and is not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.
$P_{0}/P_{1}$ gives on the $+$ strand

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(P_{0},P_{1})=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111, $

i.e. the whole $F_{2}$ haploid pool.  Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is
$s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ and contains no $1\to0$ descent.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.
Let $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$, $b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}
\in{\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$ and let the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ cut be $k$.
Then

$$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$$

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  The only $1\to0$ descent that can be created in
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the possible descent at the junction
$k|k+1$ and it can occur at most once.  Up to the fixed orientation every
attainable $+$ strand $F_{3}$ gamete is

$$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.  The zero–descent case $c=0$ is the $F_{2}$
pool $N_{0}=n+1$.

For a non-monotone word $b>0,c>0$.  Put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed $+$
orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

distinct haploid sequences can be made by two successive directed
one-break meioses.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$,
and

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26 $$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,
the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.
The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first
require a second oriented splice and appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ oriented haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent orientation-fixed
closure.  Allowing the reciprocal $F_{1}$ phase $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ to be
counted as distinct on the same formal strand this is the familiar
$2^{5}-2=30$ phased haplotype, $465$ unordered diploid, count.

*Remark.*  With the strict obligate interior cut $1\le k\le n-1$ the
formal terminal products $k=0,n$ are removed.  The $+$ strand $F_{3}$
haplotypes then necessarily start $0$ and end $1$, $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haploid types
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, $8^{2}=64$ ordered
and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes, the textbook
obligate-crossover limit. ∎

Write the two founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand as A = 0⁵ and B = 1⁵ and with the stated one-way asymmetry let the only gamete that is seen on the + strand from a heterozygote a/b be the ordered splice

R_k(a,b)= a_{1…k} b_{k+1…5},   0 ≤ k ≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal b_{1…k}a_{k+1…5} is the same physical meiosis read on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand we are asked to consider.

F1 → F2. A/B gives on the + strand

H1 = R_k(A,B)= {0^{k}1^{5−k} : 0 ≤ k ≤5}
    = 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,

|H1| = n+1 = 6 monotone 0*1* words. Every F2 chromosome is a/b with a,b∈H1 and is therefore monotone, i.e. contains no 1→0 descent.   s_{t1}               if k ≥ t2

N1(n)= #{a,b′,c′,d ≥0 : a+b′+c′+d = n−2}= C(n+1,3).

N0 =6, N1 = C(6,3)=20 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5−p)=4+6+6+4,

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put

$A=0^{5}\equiv00000,\qquad B=1^{5}\equiv11111$

and for an ordered pair $a,b$ let the directed obligate one break that is
seen on the $+$ strand be

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots 5},\qquad0\le k\le5$,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.  The
reciprocal $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the
complementary strand and is not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}
   =\{11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ $+$ strand gamete pool.  Every
$F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ with $s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}
\in{\cal H}_{1}$ and is therefore monotone, i.e. it has no $1\to0$
descent on the $+$ strand. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal
products of the same $F_{1}$ meioses.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$

Put $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}
\in{\cal H}_{1}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so the left $k$-block and the right $5-k$-block are each monotone
$0^{*}1^{*}$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can acquire a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the
fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone zero-descent words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$
pool.  For a non-monotone word $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  For a fixed cut $p$ there are
$p(n-p)$ one-descent words with the descent at $p$.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=
\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4,$

the twenty valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc., together with the six
$F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.

Hence on the strictly orientation-fixed $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can segregate in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents,
$10101$, $01010$, etc., first require a second oriented splice and
appear in $F_{4}$; $2^{5}=32$ is one descent short of saturation.

In diploid terms the $26$ oriented haplotypes can be paired to give
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal chromosomes and

$\displaystyle \frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent closure on the fixed
$+$ strand.  The often quoted $2^{5}-2=30$ haplotype/$465$ unordered
diploid count is the phase-unrestricted count obtained by admitting
both $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ as distinct $+$ strand $F_{1}$
haplotypes, i.e. by re-introducing the reciprocal orientation that the
stated strand asymmetry explicitly forbids. ∎

$$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
$R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis on the opposite strand and
is not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$.  $A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

$${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}
      =11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000 ,$$

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words.  Every $F_{2}$
chromosome is $s_{t}/s_{u}$, $s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}\in{\cal H}_{1}$, and is
hence monotone and contains no $1\to0$ descent.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$
words are the reciprocal products of the same meioses on the $-$
strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.  Put $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}}$,
$b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$. Then

$$
R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}
$$

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can contain a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the
fixed orientation

$$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

is the whole attainable set, i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with
$\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1=6$ monotone zero-descent words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$
pool.  For a one-descent word $b>0,\;c>0$ put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can be made by two successive
directed one-break meioses.

$$N_{0}=6,\qquad N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20
      =\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p),$$

the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.  The two founders are
included.  The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc.,
require a second oriented splice and first appear in $F_{4}$.

Hence
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$
different $+$ strand haploid sequences can segregate in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  In diploid terms the 26 haplotypes pair to
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, 26 homozygous and 325
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed
closure.  The often quoted $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid
count is obtained if the reciprocal $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products are
counted as distinct on the same nominal $+$ strand, i.e. with the
phase of the first meiosis unrestricted. ∎

The directed one-break is the whole story once the orientation is fixed. On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two inbred founders are

A = 0⁵ ,  B = 1⁵

and with the stated strand asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the + strand from a heterozygote a/b is the ordered mosaic

Rₖ(a,b)= a₁…ₖ bₖ₊₁…₅ ,   0 ≤ k ≤ 5 ,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. The reciprocal b₁…ₖ aₖ₊₁…₅ is the same physical meiosis read on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

F₁ → F₂.  A/B gives on the + strand

ℋ₁ = Rₖ(A,B) = {0ᵏ1⁵⁻ᵏ : 0 ≤ k ≤ 5}

= 11111, 01111, 00111, 00011, 00001, 00000,

n+1 = 6 monotone 0*1* words. The 1ᵏ0⁵⁻ᵏ words are the reciprocal products of the same meioses. With sufficient asymmetry in only one orientation they are not distinct + strand haplotypes. Every F₂ chromosome is therefore monotone and contains no 1→0 descent.

F₂ → F₃.  Let a = 0^{t₁}1^{5-t₁}, b = 0^{t₂}1^{5-t₂} ∈ ℋ₁ with t₁ ≤ t₂. Then

Rₖ(a,b)=
 s_{t₂}          if k ≤ t₁,
 s_{t₁}          if k ≥ t₂,
 0^{t₁}1^{k-t₁}0^{t₂-k}1^{5-t₂}   if t₁ < k < t₂ .

w = 0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},  a+b+c+d = 5,

i.e. the binary words of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent. The zero-descent set is

N₀ = n+1 = 6,   0^{t}1^{5-t}.

For a one-descent word b>0, c>0. Put b' = b-1, c' = c-1 ≥0, then a+b'+c'+d = n-2 and

N₁(n)= #{a,b',c',d ≥0 : a+b'+c'+d = n-2}= C(n+1,3).

N₁ = C(6,3)=20 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4,

|ℋ₃⁺| = N₀+N₁ = n+1+ C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

distinct haploid + strand sequences can be carried by an F₃ chromosome, the six F₂ monotone haplotypes

00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes new in F₃. The two founders are included.

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  The only $1\to0$ descent that can be created in
the $F_{2}\to F_{3}$ meiosis is the possible descent at the junction
$k|k+1$ and it can occur at most once.  Up to the fixed orientation every
attainable $+$ strand $F_{3}$ gamete is

$$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$$

with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.  The zero–descent case $c=0$ is the $F_{2}$
pool $N_{0}=n+1$.

For a non-monotone word $b>0,c>0$.  Put $b'=b-1$, $c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a,b',c',d\ge0:a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent.  Hence on the fixed $+$
orientation

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$$

distinct haploid sequences can be made by two successive directed
one-break meioses.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20$, $\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=20$,
and

$$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26 $$

different $+$ strand haplotypes can be carried by an $F_{3}$ chromosome,
the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ haplotypes

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

together with the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101=001|01$, $01011$, $01101$, etc.
The six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first
require a second oriented splice and appear in $F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ oriented haplotypes can be paired.  There are
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$$\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent orientation-fixed
closure.  Allowing the reciprocal $F_{1}$ phase $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ to be
counted as distinct on the same formal strand this is the familiar
$2^{5}-2=30$ phased haplotype, $465$ unordered diploid, count.

*Remark.*  With the strict obligate interior cut $1\le k\le n-1$ the
formal terminal products $k=0,n$ are removed.  The $+$ strand $F_{3}$
haplotypes then necessarily start $0$ and end $1$, $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=2^{3}=8$ haploid types
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$, $8^{2}=64$ ordered
and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes, the textbook
obligate-crossover limit. ∎

the n+1=6 monotone 0*1* words

4.text:
On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put the founders

$A=0^{5},\qquad B=1^{5}$

and with the stated one–way asymmetry let the gamete that is seen on
the $+$ strand from an ordered heterozygote $a/b$ be the directed
splice

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
$R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the $-$ strand and is
not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$

is the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ $+$ strand gamete pool

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$, $s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$.

Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ and is monotone, i.e.
it contains no $1\to0$ descent on the $+$ strand.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$
words are the reciprocal products of the same $F_{1}$ meioses.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$
Let $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}
\in {\cal H}_{1}$, $t_{1}\le t_{2}$. Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can acquire a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to
the fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

is the whole attainable set, i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with
$\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}(n)=n+1$ monotone zero-descent words.  For a one-descent word
$b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$; then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, $N_{1,p}=p(n-p)$ of them with
the descent at $p$.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $\;N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4$,

the six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes
$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$
and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}},\;0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101,01011,01101$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can be carried by an $F_{3}$
chromosome. The two founders $00000,11111$ are included and the six
$5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first appear in
$F_{4}$.

In diploid terms the 26 oriented haplotypes pair to
$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal autosomes and

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, 26 homozygous and 325
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent orientation-fixed
closure on the chosen $+$ strand.  The phase-unrestricted
$2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count is recovered if the
reciprocal $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products are admitted as distinct on
the same nominal $+$ strand.

PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the arbitrarily chosen + strand the two founders are A=0^5 and B=1^5 and with the stated one-way asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the + strand from an ordered heterozygote a/b is the directed mosaic

R_k(a,b)=a_{1…k}b_{k+1…5}, 0≤k≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. R_k(b,a) is the same physical meiosis read on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand we are asked for.

F1→F2. A/B gives on the + strand

H1 = R_k(A,B) = {0^k1^{5-k}:0≤k≤5}
 = 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,

|H1|=n+1=6 monotone 0*1* words s_t=0^t1^{5-t}. The 1^k0^{5-k} words are the reciprocal products of the same meioses and belong to the opposite strand. Every F2 chromosome is s_{t1}/s_{t2} and is monotone, i.e. contains no 1→0 descent on the + strand.

F2→F3. Let a=s_{t1}, b=s_{t2}∈H1 with t1≤t2. Then

R_k(a,b)=
 s_{t2}             if k≤t1
 s_{t1}             if k≥t2
 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2}   if t1<k<t2

so the left k-mer and the right 5-k-mer are themselves monotone 0*1*. An F3 + strand gamete can therefore acquire a 1→0 descent only at the junction k|k+1 and at most once. Up to the fixed orientation every attainable word is

w=0^a1^b0^c1^d, a+b+c+d=5,

with ≤1 1→0 descent.

N0=n+1=6 monotone zero-descent words are the F2 pool. For a one-descent word b>0,c>0 put b'=b-1,c'=c-1≥0, then a+b'+c'+d=n-2 and

N1(n)=#{a+b'+c'+d=n-2}=C(n+1,3).

For n=5

N0=6, N1=C(6,3)=20= Σ_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4,

the twenty valley haplotypes 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} with 0≤t1<k<t2≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01, 01011, 01101. The six F2 monotone haplotypes 00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111 are included and the two founders are included.

On the arbitrarily chosen $+$ strand put the founders

$a/b$ be the directed splice

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad0\le k\le5,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$

it contains no $1\to0$ descent on the $+$ strand. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$
words are the reciprocal products of the same $F_{1}$ meioses.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$.

Put $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}
\in{\cal H}_{1}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\ 
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\ 
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  An $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can therefore
acquire a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.
Up to the fixed orientation

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

i.e. the binary words of length $5$ with $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}(n)=n+1$ monotone zero-descent words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$ are the $F_{2}$
pool.  For a one-descent word $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$.
Then $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, $N_{1,p}=p(n-p)$ of them with the
descent at $p$.

For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)=4+6+6+4,$

the six $F_{2}$ monotone $0^{t}1^{5-t}$

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$, $0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$,
e.g. $00101,01011,01101$.  The two founders are included.  The six
$5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., need a second
oriented splice and first appear in $F_{4}$.

Hence on the strictly orientation-fixed $+$ strand

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}=6+20=26$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can segregate in the $F_{3}$
gamete pool.  This is the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent closure.

In diploid terms the 26 oriented haplotypes pair to

$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal autosomes and

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous.

The familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid, $465$ unordered diploid, count is
the phase-unrestricted count obtained by admitting the reciprocal
$1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products as distinct $+$ strand haplotypes,
i.e. by re-introducing the opposite-strand phase that the stated
sufficient asymmetry explicitly forbids. ∎

I’m signing on to the oriented, fixed-strand counting that is now on the table.

Put the two inbred founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand as

A = 0⁵,  B = 1⁵

and with the stated one-way asymmetry the gamete that is seen on the + strand from an ordered heterozygote a/b is the directed splice

R_k(a,b)= a_{1…k} b_{k+1…5},   0 ≤ k ≤5,

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second. R_k(b,a) is the same physical meiosis read on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand we are asked for.

F1 → F2
A/B gives on the + strand

H1 = R_k(A,B)= {0^k1^{5-k} :0≤k≤5}
   = 11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000,

|H1| = n+1 =6 monotone 0*1* words s_t =0^t1^{5-t}. Every F2 chromosome is s_{t1}/s_{t2} and is therefore monotone, with no 1→0 descent on the + strand. The 1^k0^{5-k} words are the reciprocal products of the same F1 meioses; with sufficient asymmetry in only one orientation they belong to the opposite strand and are not distinct + strand haplotypes.

F2 → F3
Let a = s_{t1}, b = s_{t2} ∈ H1 with t1 ≤ t2. Then

R_k(a,b)=
  s_{t2}               if k ≤ t1
  s_{t1}               if k ≥ t2
  0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2}   if t1<k<t2,

so the left k-mer and the right 5−k-mer are themselves monotone 0*1*. An F3 + strand gamete can therefore acquire a 1→0 descent only at the junction k|k+1 and at most once. Up to the fixed orientation every attainable word is

w = 0^a1^b0^c1^d,   a+b+c+d =5,

i.e. binary words of length 5 with ≤1 1→0 descent.

N0 = n+1 =6 monotone zero-descent words 0^t1^{5-t} are the F2 pool.
For a one-descent word b>0,c>0 put b’=b−1, c’=c−1 ≥0, then a+b’+c’+d = n−2 and

N1(n)= #{a,b’,c’,d ≥0 : a+b’+c’+d = n−2}= C(n+1,3).

For n=5

N0 =6, N1 = C(6,3)=20 = Σ_{p=1}^{4} p(5-p)=4+6+6+4,

the twenty valley haplotypes 0^{t1}1^{k-t1}0^{t2-k}1^{5-t2} with 0≤t1<k<t2≤5, e.g. 00101=001|01, 01011, 01101, etc., together with the six F2 monotone haplotypes

00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111.

|H3+| = N0+N1 = n+1+ C(n+1,3)=6+20=26

distinct haploid + strand sequences can segregate in F3. The two founders are included and the six 5-mers with ≥2 1→0 descents, 10101 etc., need a second oriented splice and first appear in F4.

On the arbitrarily chosen + strand put

$A=0^{5}\equiv00000$ , $B=1^{5}\equiv11111$

and with the one way asymmetry let the gamete that is seen on the +
strand from an ordered heterozygote $a/b$ be the directed one break

$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5},\qquad 0\le k\le5 ,$

left block from the first homologue, right block from the second.
$R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis read on the $-$ strand and is
not scored on the fixed $+$ strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$

$A/B$ gives on the $+$ strand

${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}$

the $n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words

$s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$ , $t=0\ldots5$,

$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$,

$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1$. Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ and
is therefore monotone, i.e. it contains no $1\to0$ descent on the $+$
strand.  The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products of the same
$F_{1}$ meioses on the $-$ strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$

Put $a=s_{t_{1}}=0^{t_{1}}1^{5-t_{1}},\;b=s_{t_{2}}=0^{t_{2}}1^{5-t_{2}}\in
{\cal H}_{1}$ with $t_{1}\le t_{2}$.  Then

$R_{k}(a,b)=
\begin{cases}
s_{t_{2}},&k\le t_{1}\\[1mm]
s_{t_{1}},&k\ge t_{2}\\[1mm]
0^{t_{1}}1^{\,k-t_{1}}0^{\,t_{2}-k}1^{\,5-t_{2}},&t_{1}<k<t_{2}
\end{cases}$

so $R_{k}(a,b)_{1\ldots k}$ and $R_{k}(a,b)_{k+1\ldots5}$ are both
monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$.  Hence an $F_{3}$ $+$ strand gamete can acquire a
$1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.  Up to the
fixed orientation every attainable $+$ strand word is

$w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d},\qquad a+b+c+d=5,$

$\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

The zero descent set is

$N_{0}(n)=n+1$ monotone words $0^{t}1^{5-t}$.

For a one descent word $b>0,\;c>0$ put $b'=b-1,\;c'=c-1\ge0$.  Then
$a+b'+c'+d=n-2$ and

$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$

words have exactly one $1\to0$ descent, $N_{1,p}=p(n-p)$ of them with
the descent at $p$.

Hence on the fixed $+$ orientation

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$

distinct haploid $+$ strand sequences can be made by two successive
directed one-break meioses.  For $n=5$

$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)
      =4+6+6+4$,

$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$,

the six $F_{2}$ monotone

$00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$

and the twenty one-descent valley haplotypes
$0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101=001|01$,
$01011$, $01101$, etc.  The two founders $00000,11111$ are included and
the six $5$-mers with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, $10101$ etc., first
require a second oriented splice and appear in $F_{4}$.  The $2^{5}=32$
binary words are one descent short of saturation in $F_{3}$.

In diploid terms the $26$ oriented haplotypes pair to

$26^{2}=676$ ordered maternal$\times$paternal $F_{3}$ autosomes and

$\displaystyle\frac{26\cdot27}{2}=351$

unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes, $26$ homozygous and $325$
heterozygous, the $n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$ one-descent, orientation-fixed
closure on the chosen $+$ strand.  The familiar $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid,
$465$ unordered diploid, count is the phase-unrestricted count obtained
by admitting the reciprocal $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ $F_{1}$ products as distinct
$+$ strand haplotypes.

*Remark.*  With the strict obligate interior cut $1\le k\le n-1$ the
formal terminal products $k=0,n$ are removed.  The $+$ strand $F_{3}$
haplotypes then necessarily start $0$ and end $1$, $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$,
i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid types,
$00001,00011,00101,00111,01001,01011,01101,01111$,
$8^{2}=64$ ordered and $8\cdot9/2=36$ unordered diploid genotypes,
the textbook obligate-crossover limit. ∎

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are $A=0^{5}$, $B=1^{5}$ and with the stated one-way asymmetry the + strand gamete from an ordered heterozygote $a/b$ is the directed splice
$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}$, $0\le k\le5$, left block from the first homologue. $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$: $A/B$ gives on the + strand
${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}=s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ and is monotone, i.e. contains no $1\to0$ descent on the + strand. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products belonging to the – strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$: with $a=s_{t_{1}},b=s_{t_{2}},t_{1}\le t_{2}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{2}}$ if $k\le t_{1}$, $=s_{t_{1}}$ if $k\ge t_{2}$,

The left $k$-block and right $5-k$-block are both monotone, so an $F_{3}$ + strand gamete can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.
Up to the fixed orientation $w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$, $a+b+c+d=5$, $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words. With $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$, $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$.
$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
Hence on the fixed + strand
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$:
$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)$,
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$.
The six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes are $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.

The founders on the arbitrarily chosen + strand are $A=0^{5}$, $B=1^{5}$ and with the stated one-way asymmetry the + strand gamete from an ordered heterozygote $a/b$ is the directed splice
$R_{k}(a,b)=a_{1\ldots k}b_{k+1\ldots5}$, $0\le k\le5$, left block from the first homologue. $R_{k}(b,a)$ is the same physical meiosis on the – strand and is not scored on the fixed + strand.

$F_{1}\to F_{2}$: $A/B$ gives on the + strand
${\cal H}_{1}=R_{k}(A,B)=\{0^{k}1^{5-k}:0\le k\le5\}=s_{t}=0^{t}1^{5-t}$,
$|{\cal H}_{1}|=n+1=6$ monotone $0^{*}1^{*}$ words
$11111,01111,00111,00011,00001,00000$.
Every $F_{2}$ chromosome is $s_{t_{1}}/s_{t_{2}}$ and is monotone, i.e. contains no $1\to0$ descent on the + strand. The $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ words are the reciprocal products belonging to the – strand.

$F_{2}\to F_{3}$: with $a=s_{t_{1}},b=s_{t_{2}},t_{1}\le t_{2}$,
$R_{k}(a,b)=s_{t_{2}}$ if $k\le t_{1}$, $=s_{t_{1}}$ if $k\ge t_{2}$, 
$=0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$ if $t_{1}<k<t_{2}$.
The left $k$-block and right $5-k$-block are both monotone, so an $F_{3}$ + strand gamete can contain a $1\to0$ descent only at the junction $k|k+1$ and at most once.
Up to the fixed orientation $w=0^{a}1^{b}0^{c}1^{d}$, $a+b+c+d=5$, $\le1$ $1\to0$ descent.

$N_{0}=n+1$ monotone words. With $b>0,c>0$ put $b'=b-1,c'=c-1\ge0$, $a+b'+c'+d=n-2$.
$N_{1}(n)=\#\{a+b'+c'+d=n-2\}=\binom{n+1}{3}$ words with exactly one $1\to0$ descent.
Hence on the fixed + strand
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=N_{0}+N_{1}=n+1+\binom{n+1}{3}$.

For $n=5$:
$N_{0}=6$, $N_{1}=\binom{6}{3}=20=\sum_{p=1}^{4}p(5-p)$,
$|{\cal H}_{3}^{+}|=6+20=26$.
The six $F_{2}$ monotone haplotypes are $00000,00001,00011,00111,01111,11111$.
The twenty new valley haplotypes are $0^{t_{1}}1^{k-t_{1}}0^{t_{2}-k}1^{5-t_{2}}$,
$0\le t_{1}<k<t_{2}\le5$, e.g. $00101$, $01011$, $01101$.
The two founders are included. Words with $\ge2$ $1\to0$ descents, e.g. $10101$, $01010$, first appear in $F_{4}$.

Diploid level on fixed + strand: $26^{2}=676$ ordered and $26\cdot27/2=351$ unordered $F_{3}$ autosomal genotypes.

The $2^{5}-2=30$ haploid $/465$ unordered diploid counts now appearing in the pool are the phase-unrestricted counts obtained by admitting both $0^{k}1^{5-k}$ and $1^{k}0^{5-k}$ as distinct + strand $F_{1}$ haplotypes, i.e. re-introducing the reciprocal orientation that the stated sufficient asymmetry forbids. With orientation fixed the $F_{1}$ pool is the six monotone $s_{k}$, not ten.

Strict obligate interior cut $1\le k\le n-1$: terminal products $k=0,n$ are removed. Then $F_{3}$ + strand haplotypes necessarily start $0$ and end $1$, $0x_{2}x_{3}x_{4}1$, i.e. $2^{\,n-2}=8$ haploid types, $8^{2}=64$ ordered and $36$ unordered diploid genotypes, the textbook obligate-crossover limit. The 26/351 count above is the current round consensus under the $0\le k\le5$ convention used by Colleagues 1,10,11,12,13,14,15,16,17,18 et al.
